mishnayos.summary: Two partners who share a courtyard and want to split it build a dividing wall right in the middle. Each one gives half of the land the wall stands on, and if the wall falls, the place and the stones belong to both.

chunks.en: Partners who want to make a dividing wall in their courtyard
chunks.st: Partners who wished to make a partition [meḥitza] in a jointly owned courtyard

words.note: People who own something together.

chunks.en: build the wall in the middle.
chunks.st: build the wall for the partition in the middle of the courtyard.

chunks.en: In a place where people usually build with rough stones,
chunks.st: What is this wall fashioned from? In a place where it is customary to build such a wall with non-chiseled stone [gevil],

words.note: Stones that were not cut smooth.

chunks.en: or cut stones, or small bricks,
chunks.st: or chiseled stone [gazit], or small bricks [kefisin],

chunks.en: or large bricks, they build with that.
chunks.st: or large bricks [leveinim], they must build the wall with that material.

chunks.en: It all follows the custom of the place.
chunks.st: Everything is in accordance with the regional custom.

chunks.en: With rough stones, this one gives three tefachim of land,
chunks.st: If they build the wall with non-chiseled stone, this partner provides three handbreadths of his portion of the courtyard

words.note: A tefach is about the width of a hand.

chunks.en: and that one gives three tefachim.
chunks.st: and that partner provides three handbreadths,
chunks.stMore: since the thickness of such a wall is six handbreadths.

chunks.en: With cut stones, this one gives two and a half tefachim,
chunks.st: If they build the wall with chiseled stone, this partner provides two and a half handbreadths

chunks.en: and that one gives two and a half tefachim.
chunks.st: and that partner provides two and a half handbreadths, since such a wall is five handbreadths thick.

chunks.en: With small bricks, this one gives two tefachim,
chunks.st: If they build the wall with small bricks, this one provides two handbreadths

chunks.en: and that one gives two tefachim.
chunks.st: and that one provides two handbreadths,
chunks.stMore: since the thickness of such a wall is four handbreadths.

chunks.en: With large bricks, this one gives one and a half tefachim,
chunks.st: If they build with large bricks, this one provides one and a half handbreadths

chunks.en: and that one gives one and a half tefachim.
chunks.st: and that one provides one and a half handbreadths,
chunks.stMore: since the thickness of such a wall is three handbreadths.

chunks.en: So if the wall falls down,
chunks.st: Therefore, if the wall later falls, the assumption is that

chunks.en: the place and the stones belong to both of them.
chunks.st: the space where the wall stood and the stones belong to both of them, to be divided equally.

mishnayos.summary: In a place where people usually fence off gardens, a neighbor must help build the fence. In open fields where people do not fence, one who wants a fence builds it on his own land and marks it as his.

chunks.en: And it is the same with a garden:
chunks.st: And similarly with regard to a garden,

chunks.en: where people usually build a fence, the neighbor must help.
chunks.st: in a place where it is customary to build a partition in the middle of a garden jointly owned by two people, and one of them wishes to build such a partition, the court obligates
chunks.stMore: his neighbor to join in building the partition.

chunks.en: But in open fields,
chunks.st: But with regard to an expanse of fields [babbika],

words.note: Open fields.

chunks.en: where people usually do not fence,
chunks.st: in a place where it is customary not to build a partition
chunks.stMore: between two people’s fields, and one person wishes to build a partition between his field and that of his neighbor,

chunks.en: the neighbor does not have to help.
chunks.st: the court does not obligate his neighbor to build such a partition.

chunks.en: But if one wants a fence, he moves in
chunks.st: Rather, if one person wishes to erect a partition,

chunks.en: onto his own land and builds it,
chunks.st: he must withdraw into his own field and build the partition there.

chunks.en: and he makes a mark on the outside.
chunks.explain: The mark shows that the wall is all his.
chunks.st: And he makes a border mark on the outer side
chunks.stMore: of the barrier facing his neighbor’s property, indicating that he built the entire structure of his own materials and on his own land.

chunks.en: So if the wall falls down,
chunks.st: Therefore, if the wall later falls, the assumption is that

chunks.en: the place and the stones are his.
chunks.st: the space where the wall stood and the stones belong only to him,
chunks.stMore: as is indicated by the mark on the wall. Nevertheless, in a place where it is not customary to build a partition between two people’s fields,

chunks.en: If they made it with both of them agreeing,
chunks.st: if they made such a partition with the agreement of the two of them,

chunks.en: they build the wall in the middle,
chunks.st: they build it in the middle, i.e., on the property line,

chunks.en: and make a mark on this side and on that side.
chunks.st: and make a border mark on the one side and on the other side.

chunks.en: So if the wall falls down,
chunks.st: Therefore, if the wall later falls, the assumption is that

chunks.en: the place and the stones belong to both of them.
chunks.st: the space where the wall stood and the stones belong to both of them, to be divided equally.

mishnayos.summary: If someone owns fields on three sides of his neighbor's field and fences them, the neighbor does not have to pay. Rabbi Yosei says that if he fences the fourth side too, the neighbor must share the cost of all of it.

chunks.en: If someone's fields go around his neighbor's field on three sides,
chunks.st: With regard to one who surrounds another on three sides,
chunks.stMore: that is, he owns parcels of land on three sides of the other person’s field,

chunks.en: and he fenced the first side,
chunks.st: and he built a partition on the first,

chunks.en: and the second and the third,
chunks.st: the second, and the third sides,

chunks.en: the neighbor does not have to pay.
chunks.st: the court does not obligate
chunks.stMore: the neighbor who owns the inner field to contribute to the construction of the partition if he does not wish to do so.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: If he went and fenced the fourth side too,
chunks.st: If he arose and built a partition on the fourth side of the field,

chunks.en: they make the neighbor pay his share of it all.
chunks.st: the court imposes upon the owner of the inner field the responsibility to pay his share for all of the partitions.

mishnayos.summary: If a courtyard wall shared by two neighbors falls, each must help rebuild it up to four amos high. If one later builds on the taller part, he must pay his share of all of it.

chunks.en: A shared courtyard wall that fell down:
chunks.st: In the case of a dividing wall in a jointly owned courtyard that fell,

chunks.he: מְחַיְּבִין אוֹתוֹ לִבְנוֹתוֹ עַד אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת,
chunks.en: they make each neighbor help build it up to four amos high.
chunks.st: if one of the owners wishes to rebuild the wall, the court obligates the other owner to build the wall with him up to a height of four cubits.
chunks.stMore: If after the wall was built one of the neighbors claims he alone constructed it and the other did not participate in its building, the latter is nevertheless

words.note: An amah is about the length of an arm, from elbow to fingertip.

chunks.en: We assume he already gave his share,
chunks.st: presumed to have given his share of the money,

chunks.en: unless the other brings proof that he did not give.
chunks.st: unless the claimant brings proof that the other did not give his part.

chunks.he: מֵאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת וּלְמַעְלָה, אֵין מְחַיְּבִין אוֹתוֹ.
chunks.en: Higher than four amos, they do not make him help.
chunks.st: The court does not obligate the reluctant neighbor to contribute to the building of the wall higher than four cubits.

chunks.en: But if he built another wall up against it,
chunks.st: But if the reluctant neighbor built another wall close to the wall that had been built higher than four cubits, in order to set a roof over the room that was thereby created, the court imposes upon him the responsibility to pay his share for all of the rebuilt wall,

chunks.en: even though he has not
chunks.st: even though he has not yet

chunks.en: yet put a roof on it,
chunks.st: set a roof over it.

chunks.en: they make him pay his share for all of it.
chunks.explain: He showed he wants to use the tall wall.
chunks.st: Since he has demonstrated his desire to make use of what his neighbor built, he must participate in the cost of its construction. If the builder of the first wall later claims that he did not receive payment from his neighbor, the neighbor

chunks.en: Here we assume he did not give his share,
chunks.st: is presumed not to have given his share of the money,

chunks.en: unless he brings proof that he did give.
chunks.st: unless he brings proof that he did in fact give money for the building of the wall.

mishnayos.summary: People who share a courtyard can make each other help pay for a gatehouse and a door, and people in a city can make each other help pay for a city wall. Someone counts as a person of the city after twelve months, or right away if he buys a house there.

chunks.en: They can make each neighbor help build
chunks.st: The residents of a courtyard can compel each inhabitant of that courtyard to financially participate in the building of a

chunks.en: a gatehouse and a door for the courtyard.
chunks.st: gatehouse and a door to the jointly owned courtyard.

words.note: A little room at the gate for a guard.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel disagrees and says:

words.note: A title for the head of the Sanhedrin.

chunks.he: לֹא כָל הַחֲצֵרוֹת רְאוּיוֹת לְבֵית שָׁעַר.
chunks.en: Not every courtyard needs a gatehouse.
chunks.st: Not all courtyards require a gatehouse,
chunks.stMore: and each courtyard must be considered on its own in accordance with its specific needs. Similarly, the residents of a city

chunks.en: They can make each person help build
chunks.st: can compel each inhabitant of that city to contribute to the building of

chunks.en: for the city a wall, doors, and a bolt.
chunks.st: a wall, double doors, and a crossbar for the city.

words.note: A bar that locks the doors shut.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel disagrees and says:

chunks.en: Not every town needs a wall.
chunks.st: Not all towns require a wall.

chunks.he: כַּמָּה יְהֵא בָעִיר וִיהֵא כְאַנְשֵׁי הָעִיר,
chunks.en: How long must someone be in the city to count as one of its people?
chunks.st: With regard to this latter obligation, the mishna asks: How long must one live in the city to be considered like one of the people of the city
chunks.stMore: and therefore obligated to contribute to these expenses?

chunks.en: Twelve months.
chunks.st: Twelve months.

words.note: Together, twelve.

chunks.en: If he bought a house to live in there,
chunks.st: But if he bought himself a residence in the city,

chunks.en: he is like the people of the city right away.
chunks.st: he is immediately considered like one of the people of the city.

mishnayos.summary: Partners can only make each other split a shared courtyard, field, garden or building if each part is still big enough to be used and keep its name. If both want to split, they may, but they may never cut up a holy scroll.

chunks.en: We do not split a shared courtyard
chunks.st: The court does not divide a courtyard at the request of one of the joint owners

chunks.en: unless there will be four amos
chunks.st: unless there will be in it four by four cubits

chunks.en: for this one and four amos for that one.
chunks.st: for this one and four by four cubits for that one,
chunks.stMore: i.e., this minimum area for each of the joint owners.

chunks.en: And not a field,
chunks.st: And the court does not divide a jointly owned field

chunks.en: unless it has room to plant nine kav of seed
chunks.st: unless there is space in it to plant nine kav of seed

words.note: A kav is a measure of seed or grain.

chunks.en: for this one and nine kav for that one.
chunks.st: for this one and nine kav of seed for that one.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says: The court does not divide a field

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.he: עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא בָהּ תִּשְׁעַת חֲצָאֵי קַבִּין
chunks.en: unless it has room for nine half-kav
chunks.st: unless there is space in it to plant nine half-kav of seed

chunks.en: for this one and nine half-kav for that one.
chunks.st: for this one and nine half-kav of seed for that one.

chunks.en: And not a garden,
chunks.st: And the court does not divide a jointly owned garden

chunks.en: unless it has room for half a kav
chunks.st: unless there is space in it to plant a half-kav of seed

chunks.en: for this one and half a kav for that one.
chunks.st: for this one and a half-kav of seed for that one.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says
chunks.stMore: that half that amount is sufficient, i.e., the

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: room to plant a quarter kav is enough.
chunks.st: area required for sowing a quarter-kav of seed [beit rova].

chunks.en: And we do not split a big hall,
chunks.st: Similarly, the court does not divide a hall [hateraklin],

chunks.en: and not a sitting room,
chunks.st: a drawing room,

chunks.en: and not a dovecote,
chunks.st: a dovecote,

words.note: A house for doves.

chunks.en: and not a cloak,
chunks.st: a cloak,

chunks.en: and not a bathhouse,
chunks.st: a bathhouse,

chunks.en: and not an olive press,
chunks.st: an olive press, and an irrigated field

words.note: A place where olives are squeezed for oil.

chunks.en: unless there is enough
chunks.st: unless there is enough for this one to use the property in the usual manner

chunks.en: for this one and enough for that one.
chunks.st: and enough for that one to use the property in the usual manner.

chunks.en: This is the rule:
chunks.st: This is the principle:

chunks.en: Anything that can be split and still keep its name, we split.
chunks.st: Anything for which when it is divided, each of the parts is large enough to retain the name of the original item, the court divides it.

chunks.en: And if not, we do not split it.
chunks.st: But if the parts will not retain the original name, the court does not divide it.

chunks.en: When is this? When they do not both want to.
chunks.st: When does this rule apply? It applies when the joint owners do not both wish
chunks.stMore: to divide the item; when only one of the owners wishes to divide the property, he cannot force the other to do so.

chunks.en: But when both of them want,
chunks.st: But when both of them wish to divide the item,

chunks.en: even with less than this, they may split it.
chunks.st: they may divide it, even if each of the owners will receive less than the amounts specified above.

chunks.en: But holy scrolls,
chunks.st: But in the case of sacred writings,
chunks.stMore: i.e., a scroll of any of the twenty-four books of the Bible, that were inherited by two people,

chunks.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁשְּׁנֵיהֶם רוֹצִים, לֹא יַחֲלֹקוּ:
chunks.en: even if both of them want, they may not split them.
chunks.st: they may not divide them, even if both of them wish
chunks.stMore: to do so, because it would be a show of disrespect to cut the scroll in half.

mishnayos.summary: A person may not dig a pit or channel right next to his neighbor's pit unless he keeps it three tefachim away and plasters it. Other things that can hurt a wall, like a mill or an oven, must also be kept a set distance from a neighbor's wall.

chunks.en: A person may not dig a pit
chunks.st: A person may not dig a pit

chunks.en: close to his neighbor's pit,
chunks.st: close to the pit of another, in order to avoid damaging the latter’s pit.

chunks.en: and not a ditch,
chunks.st: And similarly, one may not dig a ditch,

chunks.en: and not a cave,
chunks.st: nor a cave, i.e., a covered pit,

chunks.en: and not a water channel,
chunks.st: nor a water channel,

chunks.en: and not a washing pool,
chunks.st: nor a launderer’s pond, which is a pit used for washing clothes,

words.note: People who wash clothes.

chunks.en: unless he moves it away
chunks.st: unless he distanced all of these

chunks.en: three tefachim from his neighbor's wall,
chunks.st: three handbreadths from the wall of another

chunks.en: and plasters it with lime.
chunks.st: and he plasters lime on the place where there is water.

words.note: A white material that seals walls so water cannot leak through.

chunks.en: We keep away olive pulp and manure
chunks.st: And one must distance the solid residue of produce that has been pressed free of its oil, e.g., the refuse of olives from which oil has been squeezed, and animal manure,

words.note: What is left of olives after the oil is squeezed out.

chunks.en: and salt and lime
chunks.st: and salt, and lime,

chunks.he: וְאֶת הַסְּלָעִים מִכָּתְלוֹ שֶׁל חֲבֵרוֹ שְׁלשָׁה טְפָחִים,
chunks.en: and rocks three tefachim from a neighbor's wall,
chunks.explain: These things get hot and can damage a wall.
chunks.st: and rocks three handbreadths from the wall of another,
chunks.stMore: as all these items produce heat and can damage the wall.

chunks.en: or he plasters the wall with lime.
chunks.st: Or, alternatively, he may plaster the wall with lime to prevent damage.

chunks.en: We keep away seeds,
chunks.st: One must likewise distance seeds, i.e., one may not plant seeds,

chunks.en: and the plow,
chunks.st: and one may not operate the plow,

chunks.en: and waste water
chunks.st: and one must eliminate urine,

words.note: A polite way to say waste water.

chunks.en: three tefachim from the wall.
chunks.st: three handbreadths from the wall of another.

chunks.he: וּמַרְחִיקִין אֶת הָרֵחַיִם שְׁלשָׁה מִן הַשֶּׁכֶב,
chunks.en: And we keep a mill three tefachim away from its bottom stone,
chunks.st: The mishna continues: And one must distance a mill from a neighbor’s wall by three handbreadths from the lower stone of the mill,

chunks.en: which is four from the top stone.
chunks.st: which is four handbreadths from the smaller upper stone of the mill.

chunks.en: And an oven: three tefachim from its wide bottom,
chunks.st: And there must be a distance of three handbreadths from the protruding base [hakalya] of an oven until the wall,

chunks.en: which is four from its rim.
chunks.st: which is four handbreadths from the narrow upper rim [hassafa] of the oven.

mishnayos.summary: An oven inside a house needs four amos of space above it, and an oven upstairs needs a thick plaster floor under it, so nothing catches fire. If it causes damage, the owner pays, but Rabbi Shimon says that if he kept these measures he does not pay.

chunks.he: לֹא יַעֲמִיד אָדָם תַּנּוּר בְּתוֹךְ הַבַּיִת,
chunks.en: A person may not set up an oven inside the house
chunks.st: A person may not set up an oven inside a house

chunks.en: unless there is
chunks.st: unless there is

chunks.en: four amos of height above it.
chunks.st: a space four cubits high above it,
chunks.stMore: i.e., between the top of the oven and the ceiling, to avoid burning the ceiling, which serves as the floor of the residence above.

chunks.en: If he was setting it up in the upstairs room,
chunks.st: If one was setting up an oven in the upper story,

chunks.he: צָרִיך שֶׁיְּהֵא תַחְתָּיו מַעֲזִיבָה שְׁלשָׁה טְפָחִים.
chunks.en: there must be a plaster floor of three tefachim under it.
chunks.st: there must be a plaster floor beneath it, which serves as the ceiling of the lower story, at least three handbreadths
chunks.stMore: thick, so that the ceiling below does not burn.

chunks.en: And for a small stove, one tefach.
chunks.st: And in the case of a stove the plaster floor must be at least one handbreadth thick.

chunks.en: And if it caused damage,
chunks.st: And if he causes damage in any case,

chunks.en: he pays for what it damaged.
chunks.st: he pays compensation for that which he damaged.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: They did not say all these measures
chunks.st: They said all of these measurements to teach

chunks.en: except to teach that if it caused damage,
chunks.st: only that if he causes damage

chunks.en: he does not have to pay.
chunks.st: he is exempt from paying, as he took all reasonable precautions.

mishnayos.summary: A person may not open a bakery, dye shop or cow barn under a neighbor's storeroom, because the heat and smell can ruin what is stored there. A neighbor can stop someone from opening a store in their shared courtyard because of the noise of customers, but not from making things at home.

chunks.he: לֹא יִפְתַּח אָדָם חֲנוּת שֶׁל נַחְתּוֹמִין
chunks.en: A person may not open a shop of bakers
chunks.st: A person may not open a bakery

chunks.he: וְשֶׁל צַבָּעִין תַּחַת אוֹצָרוֹ שֶׁל חֲבֵרוֹ.
chunks.en: or of dyers under his neighbor's storeroom,
chunks.st: or a dye shop beneath the storeroom of another,

words.note: People who color cloth.

chunks.en: and not a cow barn.
chunks.st: and he may not establish a cattle barn
chunks.stMore: there, as these produce heat, smoke, and odors, which rise and damage the items in the storeroom.

chunks.en: In truth, under a wine storeroom they allowed it,

chunks.en: but not a cow barn.

chunks.en: A store in the courtyard:
chunks.st: If a resident wants to open a store in his courtyard,

chunks.en: a neighbor can stop him and say to him,
chunks.st: his neighbor can protest to prevent him from doing so and say to him:

chunks.st: I am unable to sleep due to the sound of people entering the store

chunks.st: and the sound of people exiting.

chunks.en: But one may make things at home,
chunks.st: But one may fashion utensils in his house and

chunks.en: go out and sell them in the market,
chunks.st: go out and sell them in the market,

chunks.en: and the neighbor cannot stop
chunks.st: and the neighbor cannot protest

chunks.en: him and say to him,

chunks.st: nor can he say: I cannot sleep due to the sound of the children.

mishnayos.summary: If someone's wall is next to his neighbor's wall, he may not build another wall close by unless he keeps it four amos away. He must also keep a wall four amos away from a neighbor's windows.

chunks.he: מִי שֶׁהָיָה כָתְלוֹ סָמוּךְ לְכֹתֶל חֲבֵרוֹ,
chunks.en: If someone's wall was close to his neighbor's wall,
chunks.st: One whose wall was close to the wall of another

chunks.en: he may not build another wall close to it,
chunks.st: may not build another wall close to the neighbor’s wall

chunks.en: unless he moves it away
chunks.st: unless he distances it

chunks.en: four amos from it.
chunks.st: four cubits from the wall of the neighbor.

chunks.en: And from windows, above them and below them,
chunks.st: And one who desires to build a wall opposite the windows of a neighbor’s house must distance the wall four cubits from the windows, whether above, below,

chunks.en: and across from them, four amos.
chunks.st: or opposite.

mishnayos.summary: A ladder must be kept four amos from a neighbor's dovecote so a wild animal cannot jump in, and a wall four amos from a roof gutter. A dovecote must be kept fifty amos from the city and from the edges of one's own land, unless it was bought that way.

chunks.en: We keep a ladder away
chunks.st: One must distance his ladder

chunks.en: four amos from a dovecote,
chunks.st: four cubits from a neighbor’s dovecote

words.note: A house for doves.

chunks.en: so that a mongoose cannot jump in.

chunks.en: and a father not in his son's property,
chunks.st: And a father similarly does not have the ability to establish the presumption of ownership with regard to a son’s property,

chunks.en: and a son not in his father's property.
chunks.explain: They use each other's things freely, so using it proves nothing.
chunks.st: and a son does not have the ability to establish the presumption of ownership with regard to a father’s property.
chunks.stMore: A husband and wife, or son and father, use each other’s property freely. Possession is therefore not indicative of ownership.

chunks.en: When is this said?
chunks.st: The mishna continues: In what case is this statement, that one establishes the presumption of ownership after profiting from the property for a certain duration, with the exception of the above people, said?

chunks.en: When someone just uses the land. But when someone gives a gift,
chunks.st: It is said in a case of one who has mere possession of the property, which does, in some cases, serve as proof of ownership. But in a case where another person gives one a gift,

chunks.en: or brothers who split up what they got,
chunks.st: or there are brothers who divided their inheritance,

chunks.en: or one who takes the property of a ger who died with no family,
chunks.st: or there is one who takes possession of the property of a convert
chunks.stMore: who died without heirs and his property is now ownerless,

words.note: A person who became Jewish.

chunks.en: if he locked a door, made a fence or broke a fence even a little,
chunks.st: as soon as one locked the door of the property, or fenced it or breached its fence even a bit,

chunks.en: this is a chazakah.
chunks.explain: Here this act makes the property his right away.
chunks.st: this is considered taking possession of the property, and it effects acquisition.

mishnayos.summary: If witnesses said someone used a field for three years, and they were proven to be lying witnesses, they must pay the owner the whole field. If different pairs testified about each year, they split the payment.

chunks.en: If two people testified about him
chunks.st: If there were two witnesses testifying on his behalf

chunks.en: that he ate from the field three years,
chunks.st: that he, the possessor of the land, worked and profited from a field for three years, and therefore has presumptive ownership,

chunks.en: and they were found to be lying witnesses,
chunks.st: and they were found to be conspiring
chunks.stMore: witnesses, as it was proven that they were not present to witness the matter about which they had testified,

words.note: Witnesses proven to have been somewhere else at the time.

chunks.en: they pay him everything.
chunks.st: they must pay the true owner of the field the full
chunks.stMore: value of the field that they attempted, through their testimony, to remove from his possession, as it is written in the Torah: “Then shall you do to him, as he had planned to do to his brother” (Deuteronomy 19:19).

chunks.en: If two testified about the first year,
chunks.st: If two witnesses testify that he worked and profited from the field during the first year,

chunks.en: and two about the second,
chunks.st: another two testify that he worked and profited from it during the second year,

chunks.en: and two about the third,
chunks.st: and another two testify that he worked and profited from it during the third,
chunks.stMore: and all were found to be conspiring witnesses, payment of the value of the field to the owner is

chunks.en: they split the payment three ways.
chunks.st: divided among them.

chunks.en: If three brothers testified, and one other person joined each of them,
chunks.st: If the testimony was given by three brothers, each of whom testify about one year, and another unrelated individual joined with each of the brothers as the second witness,

chunks.en: these are three separate testimonies,
chunks.st: these are three distinct testimonies
chunks.stMore: and they are accepted by the court. If they were to be considered one testimony, it would not be accepted, as brothers may not testify together.

chunks.en: but they are one testimony for being lying witnesses.
chunks.st: But they are one testimony for the purpose of rendering them as conspiring
chunks.stMore: witnesses, and the payment is divided among them.

mishnayos.summary: Some uses of a shared courtyard show ownership and some do not. Keeping an animal or an oven there is not a chazakah, but building a wall or a special place for them is.

chunks.en: These are things that make a chazakah,
chunks.st: These are uses of property that have the means to establish the presumption of ownership,

chunks.en: and these are things that do not make a chazakah.
chunks.st: and these are uses of property that do not have the means to establish the presumption of ownership:

chunks.en: If he kept an animal in the courtyard,
chunks.st: If one would stand an animal in a courtyard;

chunks.en: an oven or a stove,
chunks.st: or if one would place an oven, a millstone, or a stove there;

chunks.en: or a mill, or raised chickens,
chunks.st: or if one raises chickens in a courtyard,

chunks.en: or put his manure in the courtyard,
chunks.st: or places his fertilizer in a courtyard,

chunks.en: it is not a chazakah.
chunks.st: these actions are not sufficient to establish the presumption of ownership.

chunks.he: אֲבָל עָשָׂה מְחִצָּה לִבְהֶמְתּוֹ גְּבוֹהָה עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים,
chunks.en: But if he made a wall for his animal ten tefachim high,
chunks.st: But if one constructed a partition ten handbreadths high to contain his animal,

chunks.en: and the same for the oven,
chunks.st: and similarly if he constructed a partition for his oven,

chunks.en: and the same for the stove,
chunks.st: and similarly if he constructed a partition for his stove,

chunks.en: and the same for the mill,
chunks.st: and similarly if he constructed a partition for his millstone;

chunks.en: or he brought chickens into the house,
chunks.st: or if one brought chickens into the house,

chunks.en: or he made a place for his manure
chunks.st: or if he fashioned a place in the ground for his fertilizer that is

chunks.en: three tefachim deep or three tefachim high,
chunks.st: three handbreadths deep or three handbreadths high,

chunks.en: this is a chazakah.
chunks.st: these actions are sufficient to establish the presumption of ownership.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches which things sticking out of a house, like spouts, ladders, windows and beams, can become a chazakah. Small things that can easily be moved do not, but bigger, fixed ones do.

chunks.en: A spout does not have a chazakah,
chunks.st: With regard to a spout protruding from one’s roof gutter draining water into another’s property, its owner has no means to establish an acquired privilege for its use,

words.note: A short pipe at the end of a roof gutter.

chunks.en: but its place has a chazakah.
chunks.st: but he does have the means to establish an acquired privilege with regard to its place, as the Gemara will explain.

chunks.en: A long roof gutter has a chazakah.
chunks.st: With regard to a gutter pipe that traverses the length of the roof, one does have the means to establish an acquired privilege for its use.

chunks.en: An Egyptian ladder has no chazakah,
chunks.st: With regard to an Egyptian ladder, which is small and portable, one has no means to establish an acquired privilege for its use.

words.note: A small ladder that can be moved.

chunks.en: but a Tyrian ladder has a chazakah.
chunks.st: But with regard to a Tyrian ladder, which is large and fixed in place, one does have the means to establish an acquired privilege for its use.

words.note: A big ladder fixed in place.

chunks.en: An Egyptian window has no chazakah,
chunks.st: With regard to an Egyptian window, one has no means to establish an acquired privilege for its use;

chunks.en: but a Tyrian window has a chazakah.
chunks.st: but with regard to a Tyrian window, one does have the means to establish an acquired privilege for its use.

chunks.en: What is an Egyptian window?
chunks.st: What is the defining feature of an Egyptian window?

chunks.en: Any window that a person's head
chunks.st: It is any window that is so small that a person’s head

chunks.en: cannot fit into.
chunks.st: is not able to fit inside it.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: If it has a frame,
chunks.st: If a window has a frame,

chunks.en: even though the head
chunks.st: even though a person’s head

chunks.en: of a person cannot fit into it,
chunks.st: is not able to fit inside it,

chunks.en: this is a chazakah.
chunks.st: one does have the means to establish an acquired privilege for its use.

chunks.en: A beam sticking out a tefach or more
chunks.st: With regard to a projection
chunks.stMore: emerging from the wall of one’s house, overhanging a courtyard,

words.note: A piece of wood sticking out from the wall.

chunks.en: has a chazakah,
chunks.st: one has the means to establish an acquired privilege for its use if it protrudes at least as far as a handbreadth,

chunks.en: and the neighbor can protest.
chunks.st: and the owner of the courtyard can protest its construction.

chunks.en: Less than a tefach:
chunks.st: If it protrudes less than a handbreadth,

chunks.en: it has no chazakah,
chunks.st: the owner of the house has no means to establish an acquired privilege for its use,

chunks.en: and the neighbor cannot protest.
chunks.st: and the owner of the courtyard cannot protest its construction.

mishnayos.summary: A person may not open new windows or doors into a courtyard he shares with others, because they need their privacy. Facing a public street, though, he may open as many doors and windows as he wants.

chunks.he: לֹא יִפְתַּח אָדָם חַלּוֹנוֹתָיו לַחֲצַר הַשֻּׁתָּפִין.
chunks.en: A person may not open his windows into a shared courtyard.
chunks.st: A person may not open his windows, i.e., build an opening in a wall to use as a window, into a courtyard belonging to partners, i.e., a courtyard in which he is a partner.

chunks.en: If he bought a house in another courtyard,
chunks.st: If he purchased a house in another, adjacent courtyard,

chunks.en: he may not open it into the shared courtyard.
chunks.st: he may not open the house into a courtyard belonging to partners.

chunks.en: If he built an upstairs room on top of his house,
chunks.st: If he built a loft on top of his house,

chunks.en: he may not open it into the shared courtyard.
chunks.st: he may not open it into a courtyard belonging to partners.

chunks.en: But if he wants,
chunks.st: Rather, if he desired to build a loft, he may

chunks.en: he builds a room inside his house,
chunks.st: build a room within his house,

chunks.en: or builds an upstairs room on top of his house
chunks.st: or he may build a loft on top of his house,

chunks.en: and opens it into his house.
chunks.st: and open it into his house, not directly into the courtyard.

chunks.he: לֹא יִפְתַּח אָדָם לַחֲצַר הַשֻּׁתָּפִין פֶּתַח
chunks.en: A person may not open a door into a shared courtyard
chunks.st: A person may not open an entrance

chunks.en: across from a door, or a window across from a window.
chunks.st: opposite another entrance or a window opposite another window toward a courtyard belonging to partners,
chunks.stMore: so as to ensure that the residents will enjoy a measure of privacy.

chunks.en: If it was small,
chunks.st: If there was a small entrance

chunks.en: he may not make it big.
chunks.st: he may not enlarge it.

chunks.en: One, he may not make it two.
chunks.st: If there was one entrance he may not fashion it into two.

chunks.he: אֲבָל פּוֹתֵחַ הוּא לִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים פֶּתַח
chunks.en: But he may open a door facing the public street
chunks.st: But one may open an entrance

chunks.en: across from a door, or a window across from a window.
chunks.st: opposite another entrance or a window opposite another window toward the public domain.

chunks.en: If it was small,
chunks.st: Similarly, if there was a small entrance

chunks.en: he may make it big.
chunks.st: he may enlarge it,

chunks.en: One, he may make it two.
chunks.st: and if there was one entrance he may fashion it into two.

mishnayos.summary: A person may not dig holes under a public road, and Rabbi Eliezer allows it if a strong covering is on top. He may not build beams or balconies sticking out over the public road, but if he buys a house that already has them, he may keep them.

chunks.he: אֵין עוֹשִׂין חָלָל תַּחַת רְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים,
chunks.en: We may not make an empty space under a public road,
chunks.st: One may not form an empty space be-neath the public domain

chunks.en: like pits, ditches and caves.
chunks.st: by digging pits, ditches, or caves.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer allows it if it is strong enough
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer deems it permitted
chunks.stMore: for one to do so, provided that he places a covering strong enough that

chunks.en: that a wagon loaded with stones can go over it.
chunks.st: a wagon laden with stones would be able to tread
chunks.stMore: on it without breaking it, therefore ensuring that the empty space will not cause any damage to those in the public domain.

chunks.he: אֵין מוֹצִיאִין זִיזִין וּגְזֻזְטְרָאוֹת לִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים,
chunks.en: We may not put out beams and balconies over a public road.
chunks.st: One may not extend projections or balconies [ugzuztraot] into the public domain.

chunks.en: But if he wants, he moves his wall back
chunks.st: Rather, if he desired to build one he may draw back

chunks.en: into his own land and puts them out.
chunks.st: into his property by moving his wall, and extend
chunks.stMore: the projection to the end of his property line.

chunks.en: If he bought a courtyard that has beams and balconies,
chunks.st: If one purchased a courtyard in which there are projections and balconies extending into the public domain,

chunks.en: it stays the way it is.
chunks.st: this courtyard retains its presumptive status,
chunks.stMore: i.e., the owner has the acquired privilege of their use, and the court does not demand their removal.

mishnayos.summary: When someone sells a house without saying more, some attached parts are not part of the sale, like a side gallery, an inner room, or a roof with a high fence around it. Rabbi Yehuda adds that a roof with a doorway shape is not sold either.

chunks.en: Someone who sells a house
chunks.st: One who sells a house
chunks.stMore: without specifying what is included in the sale

chunks.en: has not sold the side gallery,
chunks.st: has not sold the gallery,
chunks.stMore: an extension built above or alongside the main building,

words.note: A narrow room built along the outside of the house.

chunks.he: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהִיא פְתוּחָה לְתוֹכוֹ,
chunks.en: even though it opens into the house,
chunks.st: and this is so even if the gallery is attached to the house and opens into it.

chunks.en: and not the room behind it,
chunks.st: Nor has he sold the room behind
chunks.stMore: the house, even if it is accessible only from inside the house.

chunks.en: and not the roof
chunks.st: He has also not sold the roof

chunks.he: בִּזְמַן שֶׁיֶּשׁ לוֹ מַעֲקֶה גָבוֹהַּ עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים.
chunks.en: when it has a fence ten tefachim high around it.
chunks.st: when it has a parapet ten handbreadths high,
chunks.stMore: as such a roof is considered a separate entity and is therefore not included in the sale of the house.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: If it has the shape of a doorway,
chunks.st: If the parapet has the form of a doorway,
chunks.stMore: that is, if it consists of two upright posts with a beam crossing over them, then

chunks.en: even though it is not
chunks.st: even if the parapet is not

chunks.en: ten tefachim high,
chunks.st: ten handbreadths high, the roof

chunks.en: it is not sold.
chunks.st: is not sold
chunks.stMore: together with the house, unless it is specifically included in the sale.

mishnayos.summary: Someone who sells a house does not sell the pit or cistern with it. Rabbi Akiva and the Sages argue whether the seller, or a different buyer of the pit, must buy a path through the other's land to get to it.

chunks.en: He has not sold the pit,
chunks.st: One who sells a house without specification has sold neither the pit

chunks.en: and not the cistern,
chunks.st: nor the cistern [dut],

words.note: A tank for water built above the ground.

chunks.en: even though he wrote for him
chunks.st: even if he writes for the buyer in the bill of sale that he is selling him

chunks.en: the depth and the height.
chunks.explain: That is, everything from the bottom to the top.
chunks.st: the depth and the height
chunks.stMore: of the house, as anything that is not part of the house, like pits and cisterns, must be explicitly mentioned in the contract or else they remain in the seller’s possession.

chunks.en: And the seller must buy himself a path to them.
chunks.st: And therefore the seller must purchase for himself a path
chunks.stMore: through the buyer’s domain to reach whatever remains his, because he has sold the area of the house along with the house itself, and he no longer has permission to walk there. This is

chunks.en: These are the words of Rabbi Akiva.
chunks.st: the statement of Rabbi Akiva.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: he does not need to buy himself a path.
chunks.st: The seller need not purchase for himself a path
chunks.stMore: through the buyer’s domain, as this is certainly included in what he has withheld for himself from the sale.

chunks.en: And Rabbi Akiva agrees
chunks.st: And Rabbi Akiva concedes

chunks.en: that when he said to him, except for these,
chunks.st: that when the seller says to the buyer in the bill of sale: I am selling you this house apart from the pit and the cistern,

chunks.en: he does not need to buy himself a path.
chunks.st: he need not purchase for himself a path
chunks.stMore: through the buyer’s domain. Since the seller unnecessarily emphasized that the pit and the cistern are not included in the sale, he presumably intended to reserve for himself the right of access to them.

chunks.en: If he sold them to someone else,
chunks.st: If the seller kept the house, but sold the pit and the cistern to another,

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says:

chunks.en: the buyer does not need to buy himself a path.
chunks.st: The buyer need not purchase for himself a path
chunks.stMore: through the seller’s domain to reach what he has bought.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: But the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: he needs to buy himself a path.
chunks.st: He must purchase for himself a path through the seller’s domain.

mishnayos.summary: Someone who sells a house sells the things that are fixed to it, like the door, but not the things that can be carried away, like the key. If he says he is selling the house and everything in it, then all of it is sold.

chunks.en: Someone who sells a house
chunks.st: One who sells a house has, as part of the sale,

chunks.en: has sold the door,
chunks.st: sold also the door,

chunks.en: but not the key.
chunks.st: but not the key.

chunks.en: He has sold the mortar that is fixed in place,
chunks.st: He has sold the mortar that is fixed in the ground,

words.note: A heavy bowl for crushing grain.

chunks.en: but not one that can be moved.
chunks.st: but not the portable one.

chunks.en: He has sold the bottom millstone,
chunks.st: He has sold the immovable lower millstone [ha’itzterobil],

chunks.en: but not the top stone,
chunks.st: but not the portable upper stone [hakelet],
chunks.stMore: the funnel into which one pours the grain to be ground.

chunks.en: and not the oven,
chunks.st: And he has sold neither the oven

chunks.en: and not the stove.
chunks.st: nor the double stove, as they are deemed movable.

chunks.en: When he said to him,
chunks.st: When the seller says to the buyer: I am selling you

chunks.en: It and everything inside it,
chunks.st: it, and everything that is in it,

chunks.en: then all of them are sold.
chunks.st: all these components are sold as part of the sale of the house.

mishnayos.summary: Someone who sells a courtyard sells the houses and pits in it, but not the things that can be moved, unless he says everything inside is sold. Either way, he does not sell a bathhouse or olive press there, and Rabbi Eliezer says he sells only the open space.

chunks.en: Someone who sells a courtyard
chunks.st: One who sells a courtyard
chunks.stMore: without specifying what is included in the sale

chunks.en: has sold the houses,
chunks.st: has sold with it the houses,

chunks.en: pits, ditches and caves,
chunks.st: pits, ditches, and caves found in the courtyard,

chunks.en: but not the things that can be moved.
chunks.st: but he has not sold the movable property.

chunks.en: When he said to him,
chunks.st: When the seller says to the buyer: I am selling you

chunks.en: It and everything inside it,
chunks.st: it and everything that is in it,

chunks.en: then all of them are sold.
chunks.st: all these components are sold
chunks.stMore: along with the courtyard, even the movable property.

chunks.en: Either way,
chunks.st: Both in this case, where he executes the sale without specification, and in that
chunks.stMore: case, where he adds the phrase that includes the movable property,

chunks.en: he has not sold the bathhouse
chunks.st: he has not sold the bathhouse,

chunks.en: and not the olive press inside it.
chunks.st: nor has he sold the olive press that is in
chunks.stMore: the courtyard, as each is an entity with a discrete purpose and not an integral part of the courtyard.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: Someone who sells a courtyard
chunks.st: One who sells a courtyard
chunks.stMore: without specifying what is included in the sale

chunks.he: לֹא מָכַר אֶלָּא אֲוִירָהּ שֶׁל חָצֵר:
chunks.en: has sold only the open space of the courtyard.
chunks.st: has sold only the airspace, i.e., the open space, of the courtyard,
chunks.stMore: but nothing found in the courtyard, not even the houses.

mishnayos.summary: Someone who sells an olive press sells the parts that are fixed in place, but not the parts that can be moved, unless he says everything inside is sold. Rabbi Eliezer says the big pressing beam is sold too.

chunks.en: Someone who sells an olive press
chunks.st: One who sells an olive press
chunks.stMore: without specifying what is included in the sale

chunks.en: has sold the base stone,
chunks.st: has sold with it the yam

words.note: The stone where the olives are put to be crushed.

chunks.en: and the crushing stone and the posts.
chunks.st: and the memel and the betulot, the immovable elements of the olive press.

words.note: The stone that crushes the olives.
Wooden posts that hold up the beam.

chunks.en: But he has not sold the boards,
chunks.st: But he has not sold with it the avirim

words.note: Heavy boards put on top of the olives.

chunks.en: the wheel and the beam.
chunks.explain: These are parts of the press that can be moved.
chunks.st: and the galgal and the kora, the movable utensils of the olive press.
chunks.basisNote: The names of the parts follow Bartenura.

words.note: A big log that presses down on the olives.

chunks.en: When he said to him,
chunks.st: When the seller says to the buyer: I am selling you

chunks.en: It and everything inside it,
chunks.st: it and everything that is in it,

chunks.en: then all of them are sold.
chunks.st: all these components are sold
chunks.stMore: along with the olive press, even the movable utensils.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: Someone who sells an olive press
chunks.st: One who sells an olive press

chunks.en: has sold the beam.
chunks.st: has sold the kora
chunks.stMore: as well, as it is the most fundamental element of the olive press.

mishnayos.summary: Someone who sells a bathhouse does not sell the boards, basins and curtains, unless he says everything inside is sold. Either way, he does not sell the water tanks or the wood storerooms.

chunks.en: Someone who sells a bathhouse
chunks.st: One who sells a bathhouse
chunks.stMore: without specifying what is included in the sale

chunks.en: has not sold the boards,
chunks.st: has not sold with it the boards that are placed on the floor,

chunks.en: the basins or the curtains.
chunks.st: nor has he sold the basins or the curtains [habilaniyot].

chunks.en: When he said to him,
chunks.st: When the seller says to the buyer: I am selling you

chunks.en: It and everything inside it,
chunks.st: it and everything that is in it,

chunks.en: then all of them are sold.
chunks.st: all these components are sold along with the bathhouse.

chunks.en: Either way,
chunks.st: Both in this case, where he executes the sale without specification, and in that
chunks.stMore: case, where he adds the phrase that he is selling everything that is in the bathhouse,

chunks.he: לֹא מָכַר אֶת הַמְּגֻרוֹת שֶׁל מַיִם
chunks.en: he has not sold the tanks of water
chunks.st: he has not sold the tanks of water,

chunks.en: and not the storerooms of wood.
chunks.st: nor has he sold the storerooms for wood,
chunks.stMore: as an explicit sales agreement is required for these matters.

mishnayos.summary: Someone who sells a city sells its houses, pits, bathhouses and other buildings, but not the things that can be moved, unless he says everything inside is sold. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says the city's guard is sold with it.

chunks.en: Someone who sells a city
chunks.st: One who sells a city
chunks.stMore: without specifying what is included in the sale

chunks.en: has sold the houses,
