chunks.he: אִם עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִתְמַלְּאָה הַמִּדָּה, לַמּוֹכֵר.
chunks.en: if it was before the measuring cup was filled, it is the seller's.
chunks.st: if the price changed before the measuring vessel is filled, the merchandise still belongs to the seller and he can cancel the sale.

chunks.en: Once the measuring cup was filled, it is the buyer's.
chunks.st: Once the measuring vessel is filled the merchandise belongs to the buyer, and the seller can no longer cancel the sale.

chunks.en: And if there was a middleman between them,
chunks.st: And if there was a middleman [sarsur] between them

words.note: A person who helps make a sale between a buyer and a seller.

chunks.en: and the barrel broke,
chunks.st: and the barrel belonging to the middleman, being used to measure the merchandise, broke
chunks.stMore: during the transaction and the merchandise is ruined,

chunks.en: it broke for the middleman.
chunks.explain: The middleman pays for the loss.
chunks.st: it broke for the middleman,
chunks.stMore: i.e., he is responsible for the ruined merchandise. The mishna teaches an additional halakha with regard to sales:

chunks.en: And the seller must let three drops drip for him.
chunks.st: And anyone who sells wine, oil, or similar liquids is obligated, after he transfers the liquid into the buyer’s vessel, to drip for him three extra drops from the measure.

chunks.en: If he tipped it and squeezed out the rest,
chunks.st: After he drips those three drops, if he turned the barrel on its side and drained
chunks.stMore: out the last bits of liquid that it contained,

chunks.en: that belongs to the seller.
chunks.st: this belongs to the seller
chunks.stMore: and he is not required to give these last drops to the buyer.

chunks.he: וְהַחֶנְוָנִי אֵינוֹ חַיָּב לְהַטִּיף שָׁלֹשׁ טִפִּין.
chunks.en: And a storekeeper does not have to let three drops drip.
chunks.st: And a storekeeper is not obligated to drip three drops, because he is too busy to do this constantly.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: On Erev Shabbos as it gets dark, he does not have to.
chunks.st: If the sale occurs on Shabbat eve as nightfall arrives, one is exempt
chunks.stMore: from dripping these three drops, as there is a need to complete the transaction before Shabbat begins.

mishnayos.summary: A father sent his small son to a store with a coin, and the storekeeper gave the boy oil and change, but the boy broke the jug and lost the coin. The Sages say the storekeeper must pay, but Rabbi Yehuda says he does not, since the father sent the boy for this.

chunks.en: Someone who sends his son to a storekeeper
chunks.st: With regard to one who sends his son to a storekeeper

chunks.en: with a coin in his hand,
chunks.st: with a pundeyon, a coin worth two issar, in his hand,

words.note: A coin worth two issarim.

chunks.en: and he measured out oil for an issar
chunks.st: and the storekeeper measured oil for him for one issar

words.note: A small coin.

chunks.en: and gave him the other issar back,
chunks.st: and gave him the second issar as change,

chunks.he: שָׁבַר אֶת הַצְּלוֹחִית וְאִבֵּד אֶת הָאִסָּר,
chunks.en: and the boy broke the jug and lost the issar:
chunks.st: and the son broke the jug and lost the issar,

chunks.en: the storekeeper must pay.
chunks.explain: He should not have given them to a small child.
chunks.st: the storekeeper
chunks.stMore: must compensate the father, as he gave the jug and coin to one who is not halakhically competent.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says he does not have to pay,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda exempts him from liability,

chunks.en: because that is why the father sent him.
chunks.st: as he holds that the father sent his son in order to do this, i.e., to bring back the jug and coin.

chunks.en: And the Sages agree with Rabbi Yehuda
chunks.st: And the Rabbis concede to Rabbi Yehuda with regard to a case

chunks.en: when the jug was in the child's hand
chunks.st: when the jug is in the hand of the child

chunks.en: and the storekeeper poured the oil into it,
chunks.st: and the storekeeper measured the oil into it

chunks.en: that the storekeeper does not have to pay.
chunks.st: that the storekeeper is exempt if the child breaks the jug.

mishnayos.summary: Sellers must clean their measuring cups and weights so that nothing sticks to them and the buyer gets less. The mishnah says how often a big seller, a homeowner and a storekeeper must clean them.

chunks.he: הַסִּיטוֹן מְקַנֵּחַ מִדּוֹתָיו אַחַת לִשְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם,
chunks.en: A big seller cleans his measuring cups once every thirty days,
chunks.explain: Leftover wine or oil sticks inside and makes the cup hold less.
chunks.st: A wholesaler [hassiton] must clean his measuring vessels, which are used for measuring liquids such as oil and wine, once every thirty days,
chunks.stMore: because the residue of the liquids sticks to the measure and reduces its capacity.

words.note: A person who sells large amounts.

chunks.he: וּבַעַל הַבַּיִת אַחַת לִשְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ.
chunks.en: and a homeowner once every twelve months.
chunks.st: And a homeowner who sells his goods must clean his measuring vessels only once every twelve months.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.en: It is the other way around.
chunks.st: The matters are reversed.
chunks.stMore: In the case of one who is constantly using his vessels for selling merchandise the residue does not adhere to the measuring vessel, and therefore a wholesaler must clean his measures only once a year. But in the case of a homeowner, who does not sell as often, the residue adheres to the measuring vessel; therefore, he must clean them every thirty days.

chunks.en: A storekeeper cleans his measuring cups twice a week,
chunks.st: A storekeeper, who constantly sells merchandise in small quantities, cleans his measuring vessels twice a week

chunks.en: and wipes his weights once a week,
chunks.st: and cleans his weights once a week;

chunks.he: וּמְקַנֵּחַ מֹאזְנַיִם עַל כָּל מִשְׁקָל וּמִשְׁקָל:
chunks.en: and cleans the scale after every weighing.
chunks.st: and he cleans the pans of his scales after each and every weighing,
chunks.stMore: to ensure that no merchandise has adhered to the pans, thereby increasing their weight.

mishnayos.summary: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says only cups used for liquids need cleaning. A seller must give a little extra when he weighs, and he must measure the way people do in that place.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:

chunks.en: When is this said? With wet things.
chunks.st: In what case is this statement, that it is necessary to clean a measuring vessel, said? With regard to moist
chunks.stMore: items, which are likely to adhere to the measuring vessels.

chunks.en: But with dry things, he does not need to.
chunks.st: But with regard to dry goods, which do not adhere to the measuring vessels, one does not need to clean his measuring vessels.

chunks.en: And he must let the scale tip down a tefach for the buyer.
chunks.st: And before adding the weights and merchandise the seller is obligated to let the pans of the scale that will hold the merchandise tilt an extra handbreadth for the buyer by adding a weight to that side.

chunks.en: If he weighed it exactly even,
chunks.st: If the seller weighed for him exactly,
chunks.stMore: i.e., with the scales equally balanced initially, instead of allowing the scales to tilt an extra handbreadth,

chunks.en: he gives him extra:
chunks.st: he must give the buyer additional amounts [geirumin],

chunks.he: אֶחָד לַעֲשָׂרָה בַּלַּח וְאֶחָד לְעֶשְׂרִים בַּיָּבֵשׁ.
chunks.en: one tenth with wet things, and one twentieth with dry things.
chunks.st: an additional one-tenth in the case of liquids sold by weight, and an additional one-twentieth in the case of dry
chunks.stMore: goods. The mishna continues to discuss the correct method of weighing: In

chunks.en: In a place where people measure with small cups,
chunks.st: a place where they were accustomed to measure merchandise in several stages with a small measuring vessel,

chunks.en: he may not measure with a big one.
chunks.st: one may not measure all the items at once with a single large measuring vessel.

chunks.en: With a big one, he may not measure with small ones.
chunks.st: In a place where they measure with one large measuring vessel, one may not measure with several small measuring vessels.

chunks.en: Where they level it off, he may not heap it up.
chunks.st: In a place where the custom is to level the top of the measuring vessel to remove substances heaped above its edges, one may not heap it,

chunks.en: Where they heap it up, he may not level it off.
chunks.st: and where the custom is to heap it, one may not level it.

mishnayos.summary: If someone sells seeds or grain and the buyer plants them and they do not grow, the seller does not have to pay, since the buyer might have bought them to eat. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says that garden seeds, which are not eaten, must grow, or the seller pays.

chunks.en: Someone who sells produce to his friend and it did not sprout,
chunks.st: With regard to one who sells produce to another that is sometimes purchased for consumption and sometimes for planting, and the buyer planted it and it did not sprout,

chunks.en: even flax seeds,
chunks.st: and even if he had sold flaxseeds, which are only occasionally eaten,

chunks.en: does not have to pay for them.
chunks.explain: The buyer did not say he wanted them for planting.
chunks.st: the seller does not bear financial responsibility for them,
chunks.stMore: i.e., he is not required to compensate the buyer. Since the buyer did not specify that he purchased the produce in order to plant it, the seller can claim that he assumed the buyer intended to eat it.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.en: Garden seeds, which are not eaten,
chunks.st: If he had sold seeds for garden plants, which are not eaten at all,

chunks.en: he does have to pay for them.
chunks.st: then the seller bears financial responsibility for them,
chunks.stMore: as they were certainly purchased for planting.

mishnayos.summary: When someone buys a large amount of food, he must accept that a small part may be dirty or spoiled. The mishnah lists how much is normal for grain, figs, and barrels of wine.

chunks.en: Someone who sells produce to his friend:
chunks.st: one who sells produce, i.e., grain, to another,

chunks.en: the buyer accepts
chunks.st: this buyer accepts upon himself

chunks.en: a quarter kav of dirt in each se'ah.
chunks.st: that up to a quarter-kav of impurities may be present in each se’a of produce purchased.

words.note: A se'ah is a measure of grain, six kav.

chunks.he: תְּאֵנִים, מְקַבֵּל עָלָיו עֶשֶׂר מְתֻלָּעוֹת לְמֵאָה.
chunks.en: With figs, he accepts ten wormy ones in a hundred.
chunks.st: When purchasing figs, he accepts upon himself that up to ten infested figs may be present in each hundred figs purchased.

chunks.en: With a cellar of wine,
chunks.st: When purchasing a cellar containing barrels of wine,

chunks.en: he accepts ten sour barrels in a hundred.
chunks.st: he accepts upon himself that up to ten barrels of souring wine may be present in each hundred barrels purchased.

chunks.en: With jugs of wine in the Sharon,
chunks.st: When purchasing jugs of wine in the Sharon region,

words.note: An area in Eretz Yisrael.

chunks.en: he accepts ten poor ones in a hundred.
chunks.st: he accepts upon himself that up to ten inferior-quality jugs [pitasot] of wine may be present in each hundred jugs purchased.

mishnayos.stIntro: When selling a significant quantity of produce or a number of items, there is a possibility that there will be a certain proportion of impurities in it or that some of the product will be of substandard quality. The mishna delineates what proportion is considered acceptable, for which a buyer may not demand compensation. With regard to

mishnayos.summary: If someone sells wine and it turns sour, the seller does not pay, unless his wine is known to go sour. If he said it was spiced or old wine, it must be what he promised.

chunks.en: Someone who sells wine to his friend, and it turned sour,
chunks.st: If one sells wine to another and then it sours,

chunks.en: he does not have to pay for it.
chunks.st: the seller does not bear financial responsibility for its loss.

chunks.en: But if everyone knows that his wine turns sour,
chunks.st: But if it is known of this seller that his wine always sours,

chunks.en: this is a mistaken sale.
chunks.explain: So the sale can be undone.
chunks.st: then this sale is a mistaken transaction,
chunks.stMore: i.e., one based upon false assumptions, as the buyer intended to purchase wine that would maintain its quality; therefore, the seller must reimburse the buyer.

chunks.en: And if he said to him,
chunks.st: And if the seller said to the buyer:

chunks.en: I am selling you spiced wine,
chunks.st: It is wine that is spiced, which is preserved and of lasting quality, that I am selling to you,

chunks.en: he must make sure it lasts until Shavuos.
chunks.st: then he bears financial responsibility to provide him with wine that will keep until the festival of Shavuot.

chunks.en: Old wine means from last year.
chunks.st: And if the seller said: I am selling you old wine, he is responsible to provide wine from the previous year.

chunks.en: And very old wine means from three years before.
chunks.st: And if he said: I am selling you aged wine, he is responsible to provide wine that is from three years earlier.

mishnayos.summary: If someone sells land to build a house for a son's wedding or for a widowed daughter, Rabbi Akiva says it must be four by six amos. Rabbi Yishmael says that is only a cow barn, and the mishnah lists sizes of houses, saying a room's height is half its length plus half its width, like the Heichal.

chunks.he: הַמּוֹכֵר מָקוֹם לַחֲבֵרוֹ לִבְנוֹת לוֹ בַיִת,
chunks.en: Someone who sells a place to his friend to build a house,
chunks.st: With regard to one who sells a plot of land to another,
chunks.stMore: with the buyer intending to build a bridal house for his son or a widowhood home for his daughter on that plot,

chunks.en: and also one who agrees to build for his friend
chunks.st: and similarly, with regard to a contractor who receives a plot of land from another under a commission to build for the owner on that land

chunks.en: a wedding house for his son
chunks.st: a bridal house for his son,

chunks.en: or a house for his widowed daughter,
chunks.st: or a widowhood home for his daughter,
chunks.stMore: the terms of the transaction are a matter of dispute. The mishna presents the dispute: In the latter case, the contractor must

chunks.en: builds four amos by six,
chunks.st: build a building that is at least four cubits by six
chunks.stMore: cubits in size, and similarly, in the case of the sale, the seller must provide a plot of land that can accommodate a building of that size;

chunks.en: the words of Rabbi Akiva.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Akiva.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yishmael says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yishmael says:

chunks.en: That is a cow barn!
chunks.st: A structure of this size is a cowshed,
chunks.stMore: and a bridal house or a widowhood home is larger than that.

chunks.en: Someone who wants to make a cow barn
chunks.st: One who wants to construct a cowshed

chunks.en: builds four amos by six.
chunks.st: builds a structure at least four cubits by six
chunks.stMore: cubits in size. The mishna delineates the standard dimensions for various other structures.

chunks.en: A small house
chunks.st: A small house is

chunks.en: is six by eight.
chunks.st: six by eight cubits.

chunks.en: A big one, eight by ten.
chunks.st: A large house is eight by ten cubits.

chunks.en: A big hall, ten by ten.
chunks.st: A banquet hall [teraklin] is ten by ten cubits.

chunks.en: Its height is half its length plus half its width.
chunks.st: The standard height for each of these structures is equal to the sum of half its length and half its width.

chunks.en: A proof for this is the Heichal.
chunks.st: There is a proof of the matter;

words.note: The main building of the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.en: Everything follows the building of the Heichal.
chunks.st: The proportions are like the building of the Sanctuary;
chunks.stMore: it was forty cubits wide and twenty cubits long and its height was thirty cubits, which is the sum of half the width and half the length.

mishnayos.summary: Someone who owns a well inside his neighbor's house may go in and out only at normal times, and may not bring his animal inside to drink. Each of them may put a lock on it.

chunks.en: Someone who has a well
chunks.st: One who has ownership of a cistern located

chunks.en: inside his neighbor's house
chunks.st: beyond the house of another,
chunks.stMore: i.e., the cistern can be accessed only by entering the property of the other, and also has access rights to that cistern,

chunks.he: נִכְנָס בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁדֶּרֶךְ בְּנֵי אָדָם נִכְנָסִין
chunks.en: goes in at a time when people usually go in
chunks.st: may enter the house to access his cistern only at a time when it is usual for people to enter,

words.note: Together: people.

chunks.he: וְיוֹצֵא בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁדֶּרֶךְ בְּנֵי אָדָם יוֹצְאִין,
chunks.en: and goes out at a time when people usually go out.
chunks.st: and may leave only at a time when it is usual for people to leave.

chunks.en: And he does not bring his animal in to drink from his well,
chunks.st: And in addition, he may not bring his animal into the house and water it from his cistern;

chunks.en: but he fills a pail and gives it water outside.
chunks.st: rather, he must fill a pail with water from the cistern and water his animal outside.

chunks.en: And this one makes himself a lock,
chunks.st: And this one, the owner of the cistern, constructs for himself a lock
chunks.stMore: on the entrance to the cistern to prevent the homeowner from drawing water from it,

chunks.en: and that one makes himself a lock.
chunks.st: and that one, the homeowner, constructs for himself a lock.

mishnayos.summary: Someone who owns a garden inside his neighbor's garden may walk through only at normal times, may not bring buyers in, and may not use it as a shortcut. If they both agreed on a side path, he may come and go as he likes and bring buyers in.

chunks.en: Someone who has a garden
chunks.st: One who has ownership of a garden located

chunks.en: inside his neighbor's garden
chunks.st: beyond the garden of another, and also has access rights to it,

chunks.he: נִכְנָס בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁדֶּרֶךְ בְּנֵי אָדָם נִכְנָסִים
chunks.en: goes in at a time when people usually go in
chunks.st: may enter his garden only at a time when it is usual for people to enter,

words.note: Together: people.

chunks.he: וְיוֹצֵא בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁדֶּרֶךְ בְּנֵי אָדָם יוֹצְאִין,
chunks.en: and goes out at a time when people usually go out.
chunks.st: and may leave only at a time when it is usual for people to leave.

chunks.en: He may not bring merchants into it,
chunks.st: Furthermore, he may not bring merchants into his garden,

chunks.he: וְלֹא יִכָּנֵס מִתּוֹכָהּ לְתוֹךְ שָׂדֶה אַחֶרֶת,
chunks.en: and he may not go through it into another field.
chunks.st: and he may not enter the garden solely in order to use it as a passageway, to enter from it into another field.

chunks.en: And the outer one may plant on the path.
chunks.st: And the owner of the outer garden may sow the path leading to the inner garden.

chunks.en: If they gave him a path from the side
chunks.st: If the court gave him an access path from the side of the outer garden,

chunks.en: with both of them agreeing,
chunks.st: with the agreement of both of them,

chunks.en: he goes in whenever he wants,
chunks.st: he may enter at any time he wants,

chunks.en: and goes out whenever he wants,
chunks.st: and leave at any time he wants,

chunks.en: and he may bring merchants into it.
chunks.st: and may bring merchants into the inner garden.

chunks.he: וְלֹא יִכָּנֵס מִתּוֹכָהּ לְתוֹךְ שָׂדֶה אַחֶרֶת,
chunks.en: But he may not go through it into another field.
chunks.st: But he may still not enter the garden solely in order to enter from it into another field.

chunks.en: And neither of them may plant it.
chunks.st: In such a case, neither this one, the owner of the inner garden, nor that one, the owner of the outer garden, is permitted to plant that side path.

mishnayos.summary: If a public path ran through someone's field and he moved it to the side, he may not take back the old path. The mishnah gives the sizes of a private path, a public road, and other paths.

chunks.en: Someone who had a public road
chunks.st: In the case of one who had a public thoroughfare

chunks.en: going through his field,
chunks.st: passing through his field,

chunks.en: and he took it and gave them a path on the side:
chunks.st: and he appropriated it and instead gave the public an alternative thoroughfare on the side of his property,

chunks.en: what he gave, he gave,
chunks.st: the halakha is that the thoroughfare that he gave them, he gave them, and they may use it.

chunks.en: and his own does not come back to him.
chunks.explain: Now the people may use both paths.
chunks.st: But the original thoroughfare that he took for himself has not reached him,
chunks.stMore: i.e., he cannot appropriate it for his personal use.

chunks.en: A private path
chunks.st: The standard width of a private path

chunks.en: is four amos wide.
chunks.st: is four cubits.
chunks.stMore: If a field owner sells the right to pass through his field to an individual, without specifying the width of the path, he must provide him with a path four cubits wide.

chunks.en: A public road
chunks.st: The standard width of a public thoroughfare

chunks.en: is sixteen amos.
chunks.st: is sixteen cubits.

chunks.en: The king's road
chunks.st: The width of a king’s thoroughfare

chunks.en: has no size limit.
chunks.st: has no maximum measure,
chunks.stMore: as the king may appropriate whatever width thoroughfare he wishes.

chunks.en: The path to a grave
chunks.st: The width of the path for the burial procession to a grave

chunks.en: has no size limit.
chunks.st: has no maximum measure.

chunks.en: The place where people stand to comfort mourners: the judges of Tzippori said,
chunks.st: With regard to the practice of standing and comforting the mourners following a funeral, the judges of Tzippori said

words.note: A city in the Galil.

chunks.en: a place for planting four kav.
chunks.st: that the standard requisite size is the area required for sowing four kav of seed.

mishnayos.summary: Someone who sells land for a family burial cave must make it a certain size, with a set number of places inside. The Rabbis argue about the sizes, and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says it all depends on how strong the rock is.

chunks.he: הַמּוֹכֵר מָקוֹם לַחֲבֵרוֹ לַעֲשׂוֹת לוֹ קֶבֶר,
chunks.en: Someone who sells a place to his friend to make a burial cave,
chunks.st: There is the case of one who sells a plot of land to another in order for him to construct for himself an underground catacomb,

chunks.he: וְכֵן הַמְקַבֵּל מֵחֲבֵרוֹ לַעֲשׂוֹת לוֹ קֶבֶר,
chunks.en: and also one who agrees to make a burial cave for his friend,
chunks.st: and similarly the case of a contractor who receives a plot of land from another under a commission to construct for him a catacomb.

chunks.en: makes the inside of the cave
chunks.st: If the size of the catacomb was not specified, then he should make the inside of each burial chamber

chunks.en: four amos by six,
chunks.st: four cubits wide by six cubits long

chunks.en: and opens up eight spaces into it,
chunks.st: and open up into the chamber, by digging into its walls, eight burial niches [kukhin] in which the coffins will rest.

words.note: Long holes dug in the wall of the cave.

chunks.he: שְׁלֹשָׁה מִכָּאן וּשְׁלֹשָׁה מִכָּאן וּשְׁנַיִם מִכְּנֶגְדָּן,
chunks.en: three on this side, three on that side, and two across from them.
chunks.st: Three niches should be opened up from the wall here, along the length of the chamber, and three from there, along the other side, and two niches from the wall facing the entrance.

chunks.en: The spaces are four amos long,
chunks.st: And these niches should be formed so that their length is four cubits

chunks.en: seven tefachim high and six wide.
chunks.st: and their height is seven handbreadths, and their width is six handbreadths.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: He makes the inside of the cave
chunks.st: He should construct the inside of each burial chamber

chunks.en: six amos by eight,
chunks.st: six cubits wide by eight cubits long

chunks.en: and opens up thirteen spaces into it,
chunks.st: and open up into the chamber, by digging into its walls, thirteen burial niches.

chunks.he: אַרְבָּעָה מִכָּאן וְאַרְבָּעָה מִכָּאן וּשְׁלֹשָׁה מִכְּנֶגְדָּן
chunks.en: four on this side, four on that side, three across from them,
chunks.st: Four niches should be opened up from the wall here, along the length of the chamber, and four from there, along the other side, and three niches from the wall facing the entrance,

chunks.he: וְאֶחָד מִימִין הַפֶּתַח וְאֶחָד מִן הַשְּׂמֹאל.
chunks.en: one on the right of the door and one on the left.
chunks.st: and one from the right of the entrance and another one from the left.
chunks.stMore: The mishna describes the general structure of the catacomb:

chunks.en: And he makes a yard at the opening of the cave
chunks.st: And he must fashion a courtyard at the entrance of the burial chamber

chunks.en: six by six,
chunks.st: that should be six cubits by six cubits,

chunks.en: as big as the bed and the people carrying it.
chunks.st: which is equal to the combined length of the bier of the deceased and those who bury him,
chunks.stMore: to ensure adequate room for the burial to take place.

chunks.en: And he opens up two caves into it,
chunks.st: And he should open up two burial chambers into the courtyard,

chunks.en: one on this side and one on that side.
chunks.st: one from here and one from there, i.e., on opposite sides of the courtyard.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: Four, one on each of its four sides.
chunks.st: He should open up four burial chambers, one on each of the courtyard’s four sides.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.en: It all depends on the rock.
chunks.st: Everything is dependent on the nature of the bedrock.
chunks.stMore: If the bedrock is hard and strong it will be able to accommodate more niches, which will be more closely packed together, with less bedrock between them. If the bedrock is softer, fewer and more sparsely spaced niches should be formed.

mishnayos.summary: If someone sells a field of a beis kor, deep holes or tall rocks in it do not count as part of the size. But if he said it is about a beis kor, they do count.

chunks.en: Someone who says to his friend,
chunks.st: If one says to another:

chunks.he: בֵּית כּוֹר עָפָר אֲנִי מוֹכֵר לְךָ,
chunks.en: I am selling you a beis kor of land,
chunks.st: I am selling you a plot of earth of the size required for sowing one kor of seed [beit kor],

words.note: A beis kor is land big enough to plant a kor of seed.

chunks.he: הָיוּ שָׁם נְקָעִים עֲמֻקִּים עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים
chunks.en: and there were holes ten tefachim deep there
chunks.st: and there on that plot there were crevices [neka’im] ten handbreadths deep

chunks.en: or rocks ten tefachim high,
chunks.st: or rocks ten handbreadths high,

chunks.en: they are not measured with it.
chunks.explain: The buyer gets a full beis kor without them.
chunks.st: they are not measured together with
chunks.stMore: the rest of the field. Rather, the buyer must be provided with land measuring a beit kor exclusive of those crevices or rocks.

chunks.en: Less than that,
chunks.st: If the crevices or rocks measured less than ten handbreadths,

chunks.en: they are measured with it.
chunks.st: they are measured together with the rest of the field.

chunks.he: וְאִם אָמַר לוֹ כְּבֵית כּוֹר עָפָר,
chunks.en: But if he said to him, About a beis kor of land,
chunks.st: But if the seller said to the buyer: I am selling you a plot of earth that is about the size of a beit kor,

chunks.en: even if there were holes deeper
chunks.st: then even if there on that plot there were crevices deeper

chunks.en: than ten tefachim,
chunks.st: than ten handbreadths

chunks.he: אוֹ סְלָעִים גְּבוֹהִין יוֹתֵר מֵעֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים,
chunks.en: or rocks higher than ten tefachim,
chunks.st: or rocks higher than ten handbreadths,

chunks.en: they are measured with it.
chunks.st: they are measured together with the rest of the field.

mishnayos.summary: If a seller promised an exact size measured with a rope, any amount too little or too much must be paid back. If he said more or less, a small difference is fine, but a bigger one must be fixed with money, or sometimes by giving back land.

chunks.he: בֵּית כּוֹר עָפָר אֲנִי מוֹכֵר לְךָ
chunks.en: I am selling you a beis kor of land,
chunks.st: If one says to another: I am selling you a plot of earth the size of a beit kor,

chunks.en: measured with a rope:
chunks.explain: That means exact.
chunks.st: measured precisely with a rope,

chunks.en: if it was even a little less, he takes off from the price.
chunks.st: and he gave him even the slightest amount less than what was stipulated, the seller must deduct
chunks.stMore: the difference from the purchase price of the field and return money to the buyer.

chunks.en: If it was even a little more, the buyer gives it back.
chunks.st: If he gave him even the slightest amount more than what was stipulated, the buyer must return the difference to the seller.

chunks.he: אִם אָמַר, הֵן חָסֵר הֵן יָתֵר,
chunks.en: If he said, Whether less or more,
chunks.st: And if the seller said to the buyer that he is selling him a beit kor of land more or less,

chunks.en: even if it was a quarter kav less for each se'ah,
chunks.st: then even if he gave him a quarter-kav per se’a less than what was stipulated,

chunks.en: or a quarter kav more for each se'ah, it is his.
chunks.st: or he gave him a quarter-kav per se’a more that what was stipulated, i.e., he gave him one twenty-fourth more or less than what was required, it is his.
chunks.stMore: The sale is valid, since the seller told the buyer in advance that he was not committing himself to precise measurements.

chunks.en: More than this, they make a reckoning.
chunks.st: If the difference is greater than that amount, he must make a calculation,
chunks.stMore: and the party that suffered a loss must be compensated. If the buyer received too much land, so that he must now compensate the seller,

chunks.en: What does he give back to him? Money.
chunks.st: what does he return to him? He returns money,
chunks.stMore: i.e., he pays the seller for the surplus land.

chunks.en: And if he wants, he gives him back land.
chunks.st: And if the seller so wishes, the buyer returns the surplus land to him.

chunks.en: And why did they say he gives back money?
chunks.st: Why then did the Sages say that he returns money to him?

chunks.en: To make the seller's rights stronger.
chunks.explain: The seller can ask for money instead of a small piece of land.
chunks.st: They said this in order to enhance the power of the seller,
chunks.stMore: and enable him to demand payment for the surplus land, rather than accept its return.

chunks.he: שֶׁאִם שִׁיֵּר בַּשָּׂדֶה בֵּית תִּשְׁעָה קַבִּין
chunks.en: Because if the extra in a field was room for nine kav,
chunks.st: As, if the surplus in the field was an area required for sowing nine kav of seed,

chunks.en: and in a garden room for half a kav,
chunks.st: and in a garden an area required for sowing a half-kav of seed,

chunks.en: or, as Rabbi Akiva says, a quarter kav,
chunks.st: or, according to the statement of Rabbi Akiva, an area required for sowing a quarter-kav of seed (see 11a),

chunks.en: he gives him back the land.
chunks.st: the buyer must return the land itself to the seller,
chunks.stMore: and the seller cannot demand payment in money.

chunks.he: וְלֹא אֶת הָרֹבַע בִּלְבַד הוּא מַחֲזִיר,
chunks.en: And he does not give back only the quarter kav,
chunks.st: And if the surplus is greater than a quarter-kav per se’a, it is not only the quarter-kav that he returns; rather,

chunks.en: but all of the extra.
chunks.st: he returns all of the surplus.
chunks.stMore: Since he is already required to make a refund, the refund must be made in the precise amount.

mishnayos.summary: If a seller uses two opposite words, like exact and more or less, Ben Nanas says we follow the last thing he said. If he sold a field by its borders, a small difference in size does not matter, but a bigger one must be paid back.

chunks.en: I am selling you an exact rope measure,
chunks.st: If the seller says to the buyer: I am selling you a plot of land of a certain size measured precisely with a rope

chunks.en: whether less or more:
chunks.st: more or less,
chunks.stMore: thereby attaching to the sale two contradictory stipulations;

chunks.en: whether less or more cancels
chunks.st: in this case, the words: More or less, nullify the words:

chunks.en: exact rope measure.
chunks.st: Measured precisely with a rope.
chunks.stMore: Accordingly, if the surplus did not exceed a quarter-kav per se’a, the sale is valid as is. Similarly, if the seller says to the buyer: I am selling you a plot of land of a certain size

chunks.he: הֵן חָסֵר הֵן יָתֵר מִדָּה בַחֶבֶל,
chunks.en: Whether less or more, exact rope measure:
chunks.st: more or less measured precisely with a rope,

chunks.en: exact rope measure cancels
chunks.st: the words: Measured precisely with a rope, nullify

chunks.en: whether less or more.
chunks.explain: We follow the last thing he said.
chunks.st: the words: More or less,
chunks.stMore: since the principle is that in all cases, one should attend to the final expression;

chunks.en: These are the words of Ben Nanas.
chunks.st: this is the statement of ben Nanas.
chunks.stMore: If one sells a field to another, telling him that he is selling him a field measuring a beit kor,

words.note: A Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: If he sold it with its signs and borders:
chunks.st: with its particular demarcations and borders
chunks.stMore: that the seller specifies for the buyer, the field’s measurement is not treated in as exacting a manner as in a standard sale. Therefore, if it later turns out that the field was not precisely a beit kor, but the difference is still

chunks.en: less than a sixth off, it is his.
chunks.st: less than one-sixth, the field is the buyer’s, and the sale is valid as is.
chunks.stMore: But if the difference is greater, e.g., one-quarter or one-fifth, then,

chunks.en: Up to a sixth, he takes off from the price.
chunks.st: until it is calculated at one-sixth, the seller must deduct
chunks.stMore: the difference from the purchase price and return money to the buyer.

mishnayos.summary: If someone sells half a field, the field is divided fairly and the buyer gets his half. If he sells the southern half, the buyer gets that half, but must give up some land for the fence and ditches between them.

chunks.he: הָאוֹמֵר לַחֲבֵרוֹ חֲצִי שָׂדֶה אֲנִי מוֹכֵר לְךָ,
chunks.en: Someone who says to his friend, I am selling you half a field,
chunks.st: If one says to another: I am selling you half a field, without specifying which half he is selling,

chunks.en: they judge the value between them, and he takes half of his field.
chunks.st: an assessment is made of the field, which is then divided between them, and the buyer takes half of the seller’s field.

chunks.en: I am selling you its southern half,
chunks.st: If the seller says: I am selling you the half that is on the southern side of the field,

chunks.en: they judge the value between them, and he takes its southern half.
chunks.st: an assessment is made of the northern and the southern sides of the field, which is then divided between them, and he takes the half on the southern side.

chunks.en: And he takes upon himself the place of the fence,
chunks.st: And he accepts upon himself to provide the space for the fence
chunks.stMore: between the two halves of the field out of his own property. He also accepts to provide out of his own property the space for the larger

chunks.en: a big ditch and a small ditch.
chunks.st: ditch and the smaller ditch,
chunks.stMore: which are meant to keep animals out of the field.

words.note: A smaller ditch.

chunks.en: And how wide is a ditch?
chunks.st: And how wide is the larger ditch?

chunks.en: Six tefachim.
chunks.st: Six handbreadths.

chunks.en: And a small ditch, three.
chunks.st: And how wide is the smaller ditch? Three handbreadths.

mishnayos.summary: Some family members inherit from each other both ways, some only inherit, some only pass on an inheritance, and some do neither. The mishnah lists which relatives belong to each group.

chunks.en: Some inherit and pass on an inheritance,
chunks.st: There are family members who both inherit from and bequeath to each other upon their respective deaths;

chunks.en: some inherit but do not pass on,
chunks.st: and there are those who inherit from certain relatives but do not bequeath to them;

chunks.en: some pass on but do not inherit,
chunks.st: and there are those who bequeath to certain relatives but do not inherit from them;

chunks.en: and some do not inherit and do not pass on.
chunks.st: and there are those who, despite being relatives, do not inherit from nor bequeath to one another.

chunks.en: And these inherit and pass on:
chunks.st: The mishna lists those referred to above. And these both inherit and bequeath:

chunks.en: A father from his sons,
chunks.st: A father with regard to his sons,

chunks.en: and sons from their father,
chunks.st: and sons with regard to their father,

chunks.en: and brothers from the same father:
chunks.st: and paternal brothers;

chunks.en: they inherit and pass on.
chunks.st: all inherit from one another and bequeath to each other.

chunks.en: A man from his mother,
chunks.st: A man with regard to his mother,

chunks.en: and a man from his wife,
chunks.st: and a man with regard to his wife,

chunks.en: and sons of sisters:
chunks.st: and sons of sisters,
chunks.stMore: i.e., nephews born to the sisters of the deceased,

chunks.en: they inherit but do not pass on.
chunks.st: all inherit from their respective relatives but do not bequeath to them.

chunks.en: A woman to her sons,
chunks.st: A woman with regard to her sons,

chunks.en: and a woman to her husband,
chunks.st: and a woman with regard to her husband,

chunks.en: and brothers of the mother:
chunks.st: and maternal uncles,

chunks.en: they pass on but do not inherit.
chunks.st: all bequeath to their respective relatives but do not inherit from them.

chunks.en: And brothers from the same mother
chunks.st: And maternal brothers, despite being blood relatives,

chunks.en: do not inherit and do not pass on.
chunks.st: do not inherit from each other nor do they bequeath
chunks.stMore: to one another, as they are not considered relatives for the purpose of inheritance.

mishnayos.summary: The Torah teaches the order of who inherits: a son comes before a daughter, a daughter before the brothers, and brothers before uncles. Whoever comes first, his children come first in his place.

chunks.en: The order of inheritances is like this:
chunks.st: The order of precedence with regard to inheritances is this:

chunks.en: As it says in Bamidbar: If a man dies
chunks.st: The verse states: “If a man dies,

chunks.en: and he has no son,
chunks.st: and has no son,

chunks.en: you shall give his inheritance to his daughter.
chunks.st: then you shall pass his inheritance to his daughter” (Numbers 27:8).

chunks.en: A son comes before a daughter,
chunks.st: This teaches that a son precedes a daughter.

chunks.en: and all the children and grandchildren of a son
chunks.st: Additionally, all descendants of a son

words.note: His children and grandchildren.

chunks.en: come before a daughter.
chunks.st: precede a daughter.

chunks.en: A daughter comes before the brothers.
chunks.st: A daughter precedes the brothers of the deceased.

chunks.en: The children of a daughter
chunks.st: Additionally, the descendants of a daughter

chunks.en: come before the brothers.
chunks.st: precede the brothers of the deceased.

chunks.en: Brothers come before the father's brothers.
chunks.st: Brothers of the deceased precede the uncles of the deceased.

chunks.en: The children of brothers
chunks.st: Additionally, the descendants of the brothers

chunks.en: come before the father's brothers.
chunks.st: precede the uncles.

chunks.en: This is the rule:
chunks.st: This is the principle:

chunks.en: anyone who comes first in inheritance,
chunks.st: Concerning anyone who precedes another with regard to inheritance,

chunks.en: his children come first too.
chunks.st: his descendants precede the other as well,

chunks.en: And a father comes before all of his children.
chunks.st: and a father who inherits precedes all of his descendants.

mishnayos.summary: The daughters of Tzelafchad got three shares of land in Eretz Yisrael. They got their father's share for leaving Mitzrayim, his share from his father Chefer, and an extra share because he was a firstborn.

chunks.he: בְּנוֹת צְלָפְחָד נָטְלוּ שְׁלֹשָׁה חֲלָקִים בַּנַּחֲלָה.
chunks.en: The daughters of Tzelafchad took three shares in the inheritance:
chunks.st: Zelophehad’s daughters took three portions of land in the inheritance of Eretz Yisrael:

words.note: A man whose five daughters asked Moshe for their father's share.

chunks.he: חֵלֶק אֲבִיהֶן שֶׁהָיָה עִם יוֹצְאֵי מִצְרַיִם,
chunks.en: their father's share, since he was one of those who left Mitzrayim,
chunks.st: Their father’s portion that he received because he was among those who left Egypt;

chunks.en: and his share with his brothers in the property of Chefer,
chunks.st: and his portion that he received with his brothers in the property of Hepher, their father;

words.note: Tzelafchad's father.

chunks.en: and since he was a firstborn, he took two shares.
chunks.st: and an additional portion that he received from Hepher because he was a firstborn, and a firstborn takes two portions of inheritance from his father.

mishnayos.summary: Sons and daughters both are part of the laws of inheritance. A firstborn son gets a double share from his father but not from his mother, and daughters are supported from their father's property but not from their mother's.

chunks.en: Both the son and the daughter are in the laws of inheritance,
chunks.st: Both the son and the daughter of the deceased are included in the halakhot of inheritance.

chunks.he: אֶלָּא שֶׁהַבֵּן נוֹטֵל פִּי שְׁנַיִם בְּנִכְסֵי הָאָב
chunks.en: except that the firstborn son takes a double share from the father's property,
chunks.st: But the difference is that the firstborn son takes a double portion of the property of the father,

words.note: A double share.

chunks.he: וְאֵינוֹ נוֹטֵל פִּי שְׁנַיִם בְּנִכְסֵי הָאֵם.
chunks.en: and he does not take a double share from the mother's property.
chunks.st: and he does not take a double portion of the property of the mother.

chunks.en: And the daughters are fed from the father's property,
chunks.st: And another difference is that the daughters are sustained from the property of the father
chunks.stMore: after he dies, as it is a mandatory condition of their mother’s marriage contract that they are to be sustained even before the estate is disbursed to the children,

chunks.en: but they are not fed from the mother's property.
chunks.st: but the daughters are not sustained from the property of the mother, which is all inherited by the sons.

mishnayos.summary: A father cannot change the Torah's rules of inheritance, but he can give his property as a gift in any way he likes. Giving everything away and leaving nothing for his sons works, but the Sages are not pleased, unless his sons did not behave properly.

chunks.en: Someone who says: This man, my firstborn son,
chunks.st: In a case of one who says: So-and-so, my firstborn son,

chunks.en: will not take a double share,
chunks.st: will not take a double portion of my estate;

chunks.en: or: This man, my son,
chunks.st: or one who says: So-and-so, my son,

chunks.en: will not inherit with his brothers,
chunks.st: will not inherit my estate among his brothers,

chunks.en: has said nothing,
chunks.st: he has said nothing,

chunks.en: because he made a condition against what is written in the Torah.
chunks.st: as he has stipulated counter to that which is written in the Torah.

chunks.en: Someone who divides his property among his sons by speaking,
chunks.explain: He gives it to them as a gift, not as an inheritance.
chunks.st: With regard to one on his deathbed who apportions his property orally, granting it to his sons as a gift,

chunks.en: and gave more to one and less to one,
chunks.st: and he increased the portion given to one of his sons and reduced the portion given to one son,

chunks.en: and made the firstborn equal to them,
chunks.st: or equated the portion of the firstborn to the portions of the other sons,

chunks.en: his words stand.
chunks.st: his statement stands.

chunks.en: But if he said it was as an inheritance,
chunks.st: But if he said that they will receive the property not as a gift but as inheritance,

chunks.en: he has said nothing.
chunks.st: he has said nothing.

chunks.en: If he wrote, whether at the beginning, the middle,
chunks.st: If he wrote in his will, whether at the beginning, or in the middle,

chunks.en: or the end, that it is a gift,
chunks.st: or at the end, that he is granting them the property as a gift,

chunks.en: his words stand.
chunks.st: his statement stands.

chunks.en: Someone who says: This man will inherit from me,
chunks.st: In a case of one who says: So-and-so will inherit from me,

chunks.en: when he has a daughter,
chunks.st: in a case where there is a daughter,

chunks.en: or: My daughter will inherit from me, when he has a son,
chunks.st: or: My daughter will inherit from me, in a case where there is a son,

chunks.en: has said nothing,
chunks.st: he has said nothing,

chunks.en: because he made a condition against what is written in the Torah.
chunks.st: as he has stipulated counter to that which is written in the Torah concerning the order of inheritance.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka says:

words.note: A Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: If he said it about someone
chunks.st: If he said this about

chunks.en: who could inherit from him,
chunks.st: one fit to inherit from him,

chunks.en: his words stand.
chunks.st: his statement stands,

chunks.en: But about someone who could not inherit from him,
chunks.st: but if it was about one for whom it was not fit to inherit from him,

chunks.en: his words do not stand.
chunks.st: his statement does not stand.

chunks.en: Someone who writes his property over to others
chunks.st: With regard to one who wrote a document granting his property to others as a gift

chunks.en: and leaves out his sons:
chunks.st: and left his sons with nothing,

chunks.en: what he did is done,
chunks.st: what he did is done, i.e., it takes effect;

chunks.he: אֲבָל אֵין רוּחַ חֲכָמִים נוֹחָה הֵימֶנּוּ.
chunks.en: but the Sages are not pleased with him.
chunks.st: but the Sages are displeased with him.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.he: אִם לֹא הָיוּ בָנָיו נוֹהֲגִין כַּשּׁוּרָה,
chunks.en: If his sons were not behaving the right way,
chunks.st: If he did so because his sons were not acting properly,

chunks.en: he is remembered for good.
chunks.st: he is remembered positively.

mishnayos.summary: A man is believed when he says someone is his son, but not when he says someone is his brother, so that man only shares from his own portion. A will found tied to a dead man is not valid unless he gave it to someone.

chunks.en: Someone who says, This is my son, is believed.
chunks.st: One who says: This is my son, is deemed credible.

chunks.en: If he says, This is my brother, he is not believed,
chunks.st: One who says: This is my brother, is not deemed credible
chunks.stMore: with regard to his other brothers’ obligation to share the inheritance with the subject of his statement. When one claims that this man is his brother, this claim is accepted with regard to the speaker’s own portion,

chunks.en: and that man takes a share with him from his own portion.
chunks.st: and the man in question takes a share of their father’s inheritance with him, i.e., from his portion.

chunks.en: If that man died, the property goes back to where it came from.
chunks.st: If the man in question dies, the property he received from the father’s inheritance shall return to its place,
chunks.stMore: i.e., to the possession of the brother who testified on his behalf, from whose portion he received a share.

chunks.en: If property came to him from somewhere else,
chunks.st: If property came into the man in question’s possession from somewhere else,
chunks.stMore: other than from the father, and the man in question died,

chunks.en: his brothers inherit with him.
chunks.st: all of the brothers of the one who testified shall inherit with the one who testified,
chunks.stMore: as according to his claim they too are the heirs of the deceased.

chunks.en: If someone died and a will was found
chunks.st: With regard to one who died, and a will written by a person on his deathbed [dayetikei]

words.note: A paper saying who gets his property.

chunks.en: tied to his thigh,
chunks.st: is found bound to his thigh,
chunks.stMore: which clearly indicates that it was written by him and was not forged,

chunks.en: it is nothing.
chunks.explain: He never gave it to anyone, so it does not count.
chunks.st: this is nothing.
chunks.stMore: The will is not valid, as he did not give it to anyone, and he may have reconsidered.

chunks.en: If he gave it over through someone else,
chunks.st: If he transferred ownership of the will to the designated recipient through another person,

chunks.en: whether to one of the heirs
chunks.st: whether one of the heirs

chunks.en: or to one who is not one of the heirs,
chunks.st: or whether not one of the heirs,

chunks.en: his words stand.
chunks.st: his statement stands.

mishnayos.summary: A father may write his property over to his son so that the son owns it but the father uses it until he dies; then neither can fully sell it. Brothers who inherit split equally, and the younger ones cannot ask for more than their father already gave the older ones.

chunks.en: Someone who writes his property over to his sons
chunks.st: A healthy person who writes a document granting his property to his sons
chunks.stMore: in his lifetime, but wishes to continue to derive benefit from it until his death,

chunks.en: must write, From today and after death.
chunks.explain: The land is theirs now, but he uses it until he dies.
chunks.st: must write: I give the property from today and after my death.

chunks.en: These are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: He does not need to.
chunks.st: He need not
chunks.stMore: write: From today and after my death; it is sufficient for him to write that the transfer will take effect after he dies.

chunks.en: Someone who writes his property to his son for after his death:
chunks.st: If one writes a document granting his property to his son from today and after his death,

chunks.en: the father cannot sell it,
chunks.st: the father cannot sell the property

chunks.en: because it is written over to the son,
chunks.st: because it is written as granted to the son,

chunks.en: and the son cannot sell it,
chunks.st: and the son cannot sell it

chunks.en: because it is still in the father's hands.
chunks.st: because it is still in the possession of the father
chunks.stMore: with regard to using the property and consuming its produce.

chunks.en: If the father sold it,
chunks.st: If the father sold the property,

chunks.en: it is sold until he dies.
chunks.st: it is sold to the purchaser inasmuch as he may use it and consume its produce until the father dies, at which point it belongs to the son.

chunks.en: If the son sold it,
chunks.st: If the son sold it during his father’s lifetime,

chunks.en: the buyer gets nothing from it
chunks.st: the purchaser has no right to use it

chunks.en: until the father dies.
chunks.st: until the father dies.
chunks.stMore: In continuation of the case discussed in the previous mishna of a father who wrote a document granting his property to his son but reserved the rights to the produce during his lifetime, the mishna states that

chunks.he: הָאָב תּוֹלֵשׁ וּמַאֲכִיל לְכָל מִי שֶׁיִּרְצֶה.
chunks.en: The father may pick fruit and feed it to anyone he wants.
chunks.st: the father may detach produce from the land and feed the produce to whomever he wishes,

chunks.en: And whatever he left already picked
chunks.st: and what he left detached at the time of his death

chunks.en: belongs to all the heirs.
chunks.st: belongs to all the father’s heirs, not only to this son.

chunks.en: If he left older and younger sons,
chunks.st: If a person died and left adult and minor sons,

chunks.en: the older ones do not get clothes from the younger ones' share,
chunks.st: the adults are not provided for by using funds of the minors,

chunks.en: and the younger ones do not get food from the older ones' share,
chunks.st: and the minors are not sustained, i.e., they do not receive food, by using funds of the adults.

chunks.en: but they split it equally.
chunks.st: Rather, they receive a share of the inheritance equally,
chunks.stMore: and each son sees to his needs from his own share.

chunks.en: If the older ones got married,
chunks.st: If the adults married,

chunks.en: the younger ones also get married.
chunks.st: the minors marry, as the Gemara will explain.

chunks.en: But if the younger ones said,
chunks.st: But if the minors say:

chunks.he: הֲרֵי אָנוּ נוֹשְׂאִים כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁנְּשָׂאתֶם אַתֶּם,
chunks.en: We will marry the same way that you married,
chunks.st: We are marrying in the same manner that you adults married during our father’s lifetime,

chunks.en: we do not listen to them.
chunks.st: the court does not listen to them.

chunks.he: אֶלָּא מַה שֶּׁנָּתַן לָהֶם אֲבִיהֶם נָתָן:
chunks.en: What their father gave the older ones, he gave.
chunks.st: Rather, whatever their father gave the adults in his lifetime he gave
chunks.stMore: them, and the minors do not have the right to receive more than their share of the inheritance.

mishnayos.summary: Daughters who inherit their father split everything equally, just like sons. One way daughters are treated more strictly is that they are fed from their brothers' share, but not from their sisters' share.

chunks.en: If he left older and younger daughters,
chunks.st: Similarly, if the father left adult and minor daughters
chunks.stMore: but no sons, in which case his daughters inherit the estate,

chunks.en: the older ones do not get clothes from the younger ones' share,
chunks.st: the adults are not provided for by using funds of the minors,

chunks.en: and the younger ones do not get food from the older ones' share,
chunks.st: and the minors are not sustained by using funds of the adults.

chunks.en: but they split it equally.
chunks.st: Rather, they receive a share of the inheritance equally,
chunks.stMore: and each daughter sees to her needs from her share.

chunks.en: If the older ones got married,
chunks.st: If the adult daughters married,

chunks.en: the younger ones also get married.
chunks.st: the minor daughters marry, as the Gemara will explain.

chunks.en: And if the younger ones said,
chunks.st: But if the minors say:

chunks.he: הֲרֵי אָנוּ נוֹשְׂאוֹת כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁנְּשָׂאתֶם אַתֶּם,
chunks.en: We will marry the same way that you married,
chunks.st: We are marrying in the same manner that you adults married during our father’s lifetime,

chunks.en: we do not listen to them.
chunks.st: the court does not listen to them.

chunks.en: This is a stricter rule for daughters than for sons:
chunks.st: This following halakha is a stringency with regard to daughters’ inheritance vis-à-vis sons’ inheritance:

chunks.en: the daughters are fed from the sons' share,
chunks.st: The halakha is that the daughters are sustained by using funds of the sons,
chunks.stMore: as stipulated in their mother’s marriage contract,

chunks.en: but not from the daughters' share.
chunks.st: but they are not sustained by using funds of the other daughters.

mishnayos.summary: When a father dies and leaves sons and daughters, if there is a lot of property the sons inherit and the daughters are fed from it. If there is only a little, the daughters are fed first, and Admon asks why the sons should lose out just for being boys.

chunks.en: Someone who died and left sons and daughters:
chunks.st: In the case of one who died and left behind both sons and daughters,

chunks.en: when there is a lot of property,
chunks.st: when the estate is large

chunks.en: the sons inherit and the daughters are fed.
chunks.st: the sons inherit the estate and the daughters are provided with sustenance
chunks.stMore: from it according to the stipulations of the deceased’s marriage contract with their mother.

chunks.en: If there is only a little property,
chunks.st: With regard to a small estate,
chunks.stMore: which is insufficient to provide for both the sons and the daughters,

chunks.he: הַבָּנוֹת יִזּוֹנוּ וְהַבָּנִים יִשְׁאֲלוּ עַל הַפְּתָחִים.
chunks.en: the daughters are fed, and the sons must ask for help at people's doors.
chunks.st: the daughters are provided with sustenance. And if the sons, who receive in this case neither inheritance nor sustenance, have no other means with which to support themselves, they go and request charity at the doors.

chunks.en: Admon says:
chunks.st: Admon says, rhetorically:

words.note: A judge in Yerushalayim in the time of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: Because I am a boy, I lose out?
chunks.st: I lost out just because I am male?
chunks.stMore: Rather, he holds that the sons also receive sustenance.

chunks.en: Rabban Gamliel said:
chunks.st: Rabban Gamliel said:

chunks.en: I agree with the words of Admon.
chunks.st: I see as correct the statement of Admon.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches about a child who cannot be called a boy or a girl, called a tumtum, and how much of an inheritance or gift he gets. It also teaches about a man who promised a gift to his baby before it was born.

chunks.en: If he left sons, daughters, and a tumtum:
chunks.st: With regard to one who left behind sons and daughters and a tumtum,
chunks.stMore: whose halakhic status as male or female is indeterminate, the halakha is as follows:

words.note: A child we cannot tell is a boy or a girl.

chunks.en: when there is a lot of property,
chunks.st: When the estate is large

chunks.en: the boys push him over to the girls.
chunks.explain: The sons inherit, so they say he must be with the girls.
chunks.st: the males direct the tumtum to the females
chunks.stMore: and exclude him from the inheritance, claiming that perhaps the tumtum is female.

chunks.en: If there is only a little property,
chunks.st: When the estate is small,

chunks.en: the girls push him over to the boys.
chunks.explain: The daughters are fed first, so they say he must be with the boys.
chunks.st: the females direct the tumtum to the males
chunks.stMore: and exclude him from receiving sustenance, claiming that perhaps the tumtum is male.

chunks.en: Someone who says: If my wife has a boy,
chunks.st: With regard to one who says: If my wife gives birth to a male

chunks.en: he will get a maneh,
chunks.st: the offspring shall receive a gift of one hundred dinars,

words.note: A hundred zuz.

chunks.en: if she had a boy, he gets a maneh.
chunks.st: if she in fact gave birth to a male, the offspring receives one hundred dinars.

chunks.en: If a girl, two hundred,
chunks.st: If he says: If my wife gives birth to a female the offspring shall receive a gift of two hundred dinars,

chunks.en: if she had a girl, she gets two hundred.
chunks.st: if she in fact gave birth to a female, the offspring receives two hundred dinars.

chunks.he: אִם זָכָר מָנֶה אִם נְקֵבָה מָאתַיִם,
chunks.en: If a boy, a maneh, and if a girl, two hundred,
chunks.st: If he says: If my wife gives birth to a male the offspring shall receive a gift of one hundred dinars and if she gives birth to a female the offspring shall receive a gift of two hundred dinars,

chunks.en: and she had a boy and a girl,
chunks.st: and in fact she gave birth to both a male and a female,

chunks.he: זָכָר נוֹטֵל מָנֶה וְהַנְּקֵבָה נוֹטֶלֶת מָאתָיִם.
chunks.en: the boy gets a maneh and the girl gets two hundred.
chunks.st: the male offspring receives one hundred dinars and the female offspring receives two hundred dinars.

chunks.en: If she had a tumtum, he does not get anything.
chunks.st: If she gave birth to a tumtum, the tumtum does not receive anything.

chunks.en: If he said:
chunks.st: If he said:

chunks.en: Whatever child my wife has will get it,
chunks.st: Whatever offspring my wife gives birth to shall receive
chunks.stMore: a gift of a certain sum, and she gave birth to a tumtum,

chunks.en: then this one gets it.
chunks.st: the tumtum receives it.

chunks.he: וְאִם אֵין שָׁם יוֹרֵשׁ אֶלָּא הוּא,
chunks.en: And if he is the only heir,
chunks.st: And if there is no heir other than the tumtum,

chunks.en: he inherits everything.
chunks.st: the tumtum inherits all of the estate.

mishnayos.summary: If older brothers make their father's property worth more before it is split, the extra belongs to all the brothers. But if they said first that they were working with their own share, the extra is theirs, and the same is true for a widow.

chunks.en: If he left older and younger sons,
chunks.st: In the case of one who died and left behind adult and minor sons,

chunks.en: and the older ones made the property better,
chunks.st: if the adult sons enhanced the property,

chunks.en: they made it better for everyone.
chunks.st: they enhanced it so that the profit goes to the middle, i.e., it is distributed among all the heirs.

chunks.en: If they said,
chunks.st: If the adult sons said from the outset:

chunks.en: See what our father left us;
chunks.st: See that which our father left behind;

chunks.en: we will work with it and eat from it,
chunks.st: we are going to engage in business with our share of the property and profit from it,

chunks.en: they made it better for themselves.
chunks.st: then they enhanced the property for themselves.

chunks.en: And also a wife who made the property better
chunks.st: And similarly, with regard to a wife who enhanced the property of her deceased husband,

chunks.en: made it better for everyone.
chunks.st: she enhanced it so that the profit goes to the middle,
chunks.stMore: i.e., it is divided between her and the heirs.

chunks.en: If she said,
chunks.st: If she said:

chunks.en: See what my husband left me;
chunks.st: See that which my husband left me;

chunks.en: I will work with it and eat from it,
chunks.st: I am going to engage in business with my share and profit from it,

chunks.en: she made it better for herself.
chunks.st: then she enhanced the property for herself.

mishnayos.summary: Brothers who share their father's property split what one of them earns from a public job, but each pays for his own doctor. Wedding gifts that the father gave can be collected back in court for all the brothers, but simple gifts of wine or oil cannot.

chunks.he: הָאַחִין הַשֻּׁתָּפִין שֶׁנָּפַל אֶחָד מֵהֶן לָאֻמָּנוּת,
chunks.en: Brothers who are partners, and one of them was called to a public job:
chunks.st: With regard to brothers who were also partners, and it occurred that one of them was summoned to public service, which is assessed per family,

chunks.en: it was for everyone.
chunks.explain: What he earns or pays is split among them all.
chunks.st: he was summoned from the middle,
chunks.stMore: i.e., the profits or expenses of his service are divided among them.

chunks.en: If he got sick and was healed,
chunks.st: If one of the brothers became sick and sought treatment,

chunks.en: he is healed from his own money.
chunks.st: the cost of the treatment is paid from his own
chunks.stMore: resources. It was common practice for friends of a groom to give him gifts in order to help cover the expenses of the wedding feast. These gifts are known as gifts of groomsmen, and would be reciprocated in turn. While the groom and the groomsman were at times the recipient and the giver of the gifts, respectively, the gifts were at times provided by the father of the groomsman and received by the father of the groom. In the case of

chunks.he: הָאַחִין שֶׁעָשׂוּ מִקְצָתָן שׁוּשְׁבִינוּת בְּחַיֵּי הָאָב,
chunks.en: Brothers, some of whom gave wedding gifts while their father was alive:
chunks.st: brothers, some of whom brought gifts of groomsmen in their father’s lifetime, which were provided by their father,

words.note: Gifts given to a groom, which he later gives back.

chunks.en: when the wedding gift comes back,
chunks.st: when the gifts of groomsmen are reciprocated
chunks.stMore: after the father’s death, when one of the brothers gets married,

chunks.en: it comes back to everyone,
chunks.st: they are reciprocated to the middle, i.e., the gift is divided among the brothers.

chunks.en: because a wedding gift can be collected in court.
chunks.st: This is because gifts of groomsmen are a legal debt owed to the father, collectible in court.

chunks.en: But someone who sends his friend
chunks.st: But with regard to one who sends his friend

chunks.en: jugs of wine and jugs of oil,
chunks.st: jugs of wine or jugs of oil,

chunks.en: cannot collect them in court,
chunks.st: a reciprocal gift is not collectible in court,

chunks.en: because they are acts of kindness.
chunks.st: because they are considered acts of kindness.

mishnayos.summary: A groom sent gifts to his bride's family's house. If the wedding does not happen, whether he can get the gifts back depends on whether he ate a meal there and what kind of gifts they were.

chunks.en: Someone who sends gifts to his father-in-law's house:
chunks.st: With regard to one who sends presents [sivlonot] to his father-in-law’s house following his betrothal,

chunks.en: if he sent there a hundred maneh,
chunks.st: even if he sent there the sum of ten thousand dinars

chunks.he: וְאָכַל שָׁם סְעוּדַת חָתָן אֲפִלּוּ בְדִינָר,
chunks.en: and ate a groom's meal there, even worth one dinar,
chunks.st: and subsequently ate there a groom’s feast even worth the value of a single dinar,
chunks.stMore: if for any reason the marriage is not effected, the presents

chunks.en: they are not collected back.
chunks.explain: This is if the wedding does not happen.
chunks.st: are not collected in return by the formerly betrothed man.

chunks.en: If he did not eat a groom's meal there,
chunks.st: If he did not eat a groom’s feast there,

chunks.en: they are collected back.
chunks.st: the presents are collected, as they were not an unconditional gift.

chunks.en: If he sent many gifts that would come back
chunks.st: If he sent many presents with the stipulation

chunks.en: with her to her husband's house,
chunks.st: that they return with her to her husband’s house, i.e., to his own house, after the wedding,

chunks.en: they are collected back.
chunks.st: these are collected if the marriage is not effected.

chunks.he: סִבְלוֹנוֹת מֻעָטִין שֶׁתִּשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בָּהֶן בְּבֵית אָבִיהָ,
chunks.en: A few gifts for her to use in her father's house
chunks.st: If he sent a few presents for her to use while in her father’s house,

chunks.en: are not collected back.
chunks.st: they are not collected.

mishnayos.summary: A very sick person who gives away all his property but keeps a little land for himself cannot take the gift back if he gets better. If he kept nothing, the gift was only in case he died, so it does not stand if he recovers.

chunks.he: שְׁכִיב מְרַע שֶׁכָּתַב כָּל נְכָסָיו לַאֲחֵרִים
chunks.en: A very sick person who wrote all his property over to others
chunks.st: With regard to a person on his death-bed who wrote a deed granting all of his property to others,

words.note: A very sick person who might die.

chunks.en: and kept any amount of land for himself:
chunks.st: and he reserved for himself any amount of land,

chunks.en: his gift stands.
chunks.st: his gift stands even if he subsequently recovers.

chunks.en: If he did not keep any land at all,
chunks.st: If he did not reserve for himself any amount of land, and he recovered,

chunks.en: his gift does not stand.
chunks.explain: This is if he gets better.
chunks.st: his gift does not stand,
chunks.stMore: as the gift was conditional upon his death, since is it evident that he did not intend to leave himself without means of support.

chunks.en: If he did not write in it that he was very sick,
chunks.st: If one did not write in the deed that he was on his deathbed,

chunks.en: and he says, I was very sick,
chunks.st: and he then recovered and wished to retract the gift, and he says: I was on my deathbed,
chunks.stMore: and since I recovered, I can retract the gift,

chunks.en: and they say, You were healthy,
chunks.st: but the recipients say: You were healthy, and the gift cannot be retracted,

chunks.he: צָרִיךְ לְהָבִיא רְאָיָה שֶׁהָיָה שְׁכִיב מְרַע,
chunks.en: he must bring proof that he was very sick.
chunks.st: the giver must bring proof that he was on his deathbed in order to retract the gift.

chunks.en: These are the words of Rabbi Meir.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: But the Sages say:
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: Whoever wants to take from his friend must bring the proof.
chunks.st: The burden of proof rests upon the claimant,
chunks.stMore: and since the property is in the possession of the giver, the recipients must bring proof that they have the right to receive it.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Eliezer says that even a sick person must give property in the usual ways, and the Sages argue. They also argue whether a person can give his property just by saying so, on Shabbos or on a weekday, and whether someone can get a gift for another person.

chunks.en: Someone who divides his property by speaking:
chunks.st: With regard to one who divides his property between various recipients by means of verbal instruction,

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Elazar says:

chunks.en: Whether he is healthy or in danger,
chunks.st: Both in the case of one who is healthy and in the case of one who is dangerously ill, the halakha is as follows:

chunks.en: land
chunks.st: Property that serves as a guarantee, i.e., land,

chunks.en: is bought with money, a document, or chazakah,
chunks.st: is acquired by means of money, by a deed of transfer, or by taking possession of it.

chunks.en: and things that can be moved
chunks.st: And that which does not serve as a guarantee, i.e., movable property,

chunks.en: are bought only by pulling.
chunks.st: can be acquired only by pulling.

chunks.en: They said to him:
chunks.st: The Rabbis said to Rabbi Elazar:

chunks.en: It once happened with the mother of the sons of Rochel,
chunks.st: There was an incident involving the mother of the sons of Rokhel,

chunks.en: that she was sick,
chunks.st: who was sick,

chunks.en: and she said, Give my pin to my daughter,
chunks.st: and who said: My brooch shall be given to my daughter,

words.note: A piece of jewelry.

chunks.en: and it was worth twelve maneh,
chunks.st: and it is valued at twelve hundred dinars.

chunks.en: and she died, and they kept her words.
chunks.st: And this woman subsequently died, and the Sages upheld her statement.
chunks.stMore: This indicates that a person on his deathbed can gift property without an act of acquisition.

chunks.en: He said to them:
chunks.st: Rabbi Elazar said to them: That case was different;

chunks.en: The sons of Rochel were not good people.
chunks.explain: So we cannot learn the rule from that story.
chunks.st: the sons of Rokhel should be buried by their mother,
chunks.stMore: i.e., he cursed them. It is not possible to bring a proof from this incident, as these sons were wicked people. Consequently, when ruling in this matter the Sages did not act in accordance with the halakha, but allowed the mother of the sons of Rokhel to give this valuable piece of jewelry to their sister without an act of acquisition having been performed.

words.note: He spoke sharply about them because they were not good people.

chunks.en: And the Sages say:
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:
chunks.basisNote: Steinsaltz's version of the Mishnah has Rabbi Eliezer saying this.

chunks.en: On Shabbos, his words stand,
chunks.st: On Shabbat, the verbal statement of a person on his deathbed stands,

chunks.en: because he cannot write.
chunks.st: as he cannot write,
chunks.stMore: and the Sages instituted that he can effect the transaction verbally lest the inability to do so exacerbate his condition.

chunks.en: But not on a weekday.
chunks.st: But a verbal instruction does not stand if stated on a weekday.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua says:

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: They said it about Shabbos,
chunks.st: With regard to Shabbat, the Sages stated
chunks.stMore: that his verbal instruction is sufficient, even though writing is prohibited.

chunks.en: so surely on a weekday!
chunks.st: One can infer a fortiori that the same applies with regard to a weekday, when writing is permitted.

words.note: Surely so; if it is true there, it is even more true here.

chunks.en: In the same way,
chunks.st: Similarly,

chunks.en: we can get a gift for a child,
chunks.st: one can acquire property on behalf of a minor,

chunks.en: but we cannot get a gift for a grown-up.

chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
